source.text: Ἦσαν δὲ αὐτῷ ἐγγίζοντες πάντες οἱ τελῶναι καὶ οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἀκούειν αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Were now to him drawing near all the tax collectors and the sinners to hear him.

en.L: Now all the tax collectors and the sinners were coming near to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to hear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Tax collectors and sinners, all of them, kept coming near to listen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Tax collectors and other people known as sinners kept crowding around Jesus. They all wanted to hear what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had to say.

es.L: Y se estaban acercando a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} todos los publicanos y los pecadores para oírlo.
es.B: Los cobradores de impuestos y los pecadores, todos ellos, se {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} acercaban una y otra vez para escucharlo.
es.R: Los cobradores de impuestos y otros a quienes la gente llamaba pecadores se amontonaban alrededor de Jesús. Todos querían oír lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} tenía que decir.

fr.L: Or tous les collecteurs d’impôts et les pécheurs s’approchaient de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} pour {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}écouter.
fr.B: Les collecteurs d’impôts et les pécheurs, tous autant qu’ils étaient, ne cessaient de s’approcher de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} pour {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}écouter.
fr.R: Des collecteurs d’impôts et d’autres gens qu’on appelait des pécheurs se pressaient sans cesse autour de Jésus. Ils voulaient tous entendre ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait à dire.

sw.L: Basi watoza ushuru wote na wenye dhambi walikuwa wakimkaribia ili kumsikiliza.
sw.B: Watoza ushuru na wenye dhambi, wote, walikuwa wakimjia mara kwa mara ili wamsikilize.
sw.R: Watoza ushuru na watu wengine walioitwa wenye dhambi walikuwa wakimzunguka Yesu kwa wingi. Wote walitaka kusikia maneno {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.

vi.L: Bấy giờ tất cả những người thu thuế và những người tội lỗi đều đến gần {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} để nghe {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Những người thu thuế và những người tội lỗi, tất cả đều cứ kéo đến gần để nghe {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Những người thu thuế và những người khác bị xem là tội lỗi cứ kéo đến vây quanh Đức Giê-xu. Tất cả họ đều muốn nghe những gì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói.

decisions.choice: all: great numbers of them, a way of stressing how many came
alternatives: every single tax collector and sinner in the land
decisions.reason: Luke often uses "all" for a large crowd (5:17; 6:19). The point is that such people kept coming to Jesus.

decisions.choice: tax collectors and sinners: people the religious leaders kept away from
decisions.reason: Tax collectors worked for Rome or its rulers and were known for taking more than was due (3:12-13). "Sinners" were people known for breaking the law or living outside its rules (5:30; 7:37).

decisions.choice: were drawing near: a scene that kept happening, not one visit
decisions.reason: The verb form pictures an ongoing state of affairs. It sets the scene for the three parables that follow.

decisions.choice: other people known as sinners
decisions.reason: Readable shows that "sinners" was a label for a group, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: publicanos (L); cobradores de impuestos (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Publicano" is the traditional name for these men (meaning decision m2) and Literal keeps it; Balanced and Readable say what they did, as through Luke.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); the parables Jesus tells in 15:4-32 are speech, in the present, conditional and passé composé at every level
alternatives: the parable of 15:11-32 in the passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: As in John and Mark: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken and read in school today. Jesus' stories are speech, so they keep the tenses of speech at every level, as the style guide asks. Ongoing scenes such as this one (m3) are in the imperfect at every level. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: les collecteurs d’impôts
decisions.reason: The term sheet's word at every level: "publicains" is the traditional term but most readers no longer know it, and "collecteurs d’impôts" says what these men did (m2).

decisions.choice: no span on "wakimkaribia", "kumsikiliza"; maneno {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} (R)
decisions.reason: Swahili marks "him" inside the verb, where no capital can go, so the deity_pronoun spans of the English Literal and Balanced have no Swahili counterpart; Readable has a free possessive and takes the span, as through Luke.

decisions.choice: "những người thu thuế và những người tội lỗi"
decisions.reason: As in 5:30.

source.text: καὶ διεγόγγυζον οἵ τε Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς λέγοντες ὅτι Οὗτος ἁμαρτωλοὺς προσδέχεται καὶ συνεσθίει αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: And were grumbling both the Pharisees and the scribes saying that, This [man] sinners receives and eats with them.

en.L: And both the Pharisees and the scribes were grumbling, saying, "This man receives sinners and eats with them."
en.B: But the Pharisees and the scribes complained among themselves. "This man welcomes sinners," they said, "and even shares meals with them."
en.R: But the Pharisees and the teachers of the law did not like it. They grumbled, "This man makes sinners feel welcome. He even eats with them!"

es.L: Y murmuraban tanto los fariseos como los escribas, diciendo: «Este recibe a pecadores y come con ellos».
es.B: Pero los fariseos y los escribas se quejaban entre sí: «Este hombre acoge a los pecadores —decían—, y hasta comparte la mesa con ellos».
es.R: Pero a los fariseos y a los maestros de la ley no les gustaba. Murmuraban: «Este hombre hace sentir bienvenidos a los pecadores. ¡Hasta come con ellos!».

fr.L: Et les Pharisiens comme les scribes murmuraient, disant : « Celui-ci accueille des pécheurs et mange avec eux. »
fr.B: Mais les Pharisiens et les scribes murmuraient entre eux : « Cet homme accueille les pécheurs, disaient-ils, et il va jusqu’à partager leurs repas ! »
fr.R: Mais les Pharisiens et les spécialistes de la Loi n’étaient pas contents. Ils ont protesté : « Cet homme fait bon accueil aux pécheurs. Il mange même avec eux ! »

sw.L: Na Mafarisayo pamoja na waandishi walikuwa wakinung'unika, wakisema, "Huyu anawapokea wenye dhambi na kula pamoja nao."
sw.B: Lakini Mafarisayo na waandishi walilalamika wao kwa wao. Walisema, "Mtu huyu anawapokea wenye dhambi kwa furaha, na hata anashiriki chakula nao."
sw.R: Lakini Mafarisayo na walimu wa sheria hawakupendezwa. Walinung'unika, "Mtu huyu anawafanya wenye dhambi wajisikie wamekaribishwa. Hata anakula pamoja nao!"

vi.L: Và cả những người Pha-ri-si lẫn các thầy thông giáo đều lằm bằm, nói rằng: "Người này tiếp đón những kẻ tội lỗi và ăn với họ."
vi.B: Nhưng những người Pha-ri-si và các thầy thông giáo lằm bằm với nhau: "Gã này tiếp đón những kẻ tội lỗi, lại còn ngồi ăn chung với họ nữa."
vi.R: Nhưng những người Pha-ri-si và các thầy dạy luật không bằng lòng. Họ phàn nàn: "Ông ta làm cho những người tội lỗi thấy mình được tiếp đón. Ông ta còn ăn chung với họ nữa!"

decisions.choice: were grumbling: the word used of Israel grumbling in the wilderness
decisions.reason: The Greek Old Testament uses this kind of verb for Israel's complaints against Moses and God (Exodus 16:7-8). Luke used it when Jesus ate at Levi's house (5:30) and will use it again at Zacchaeus' house (19:7).

decisions.choice: the Pharisees and the scribes: a Jewish movement devoted to keeping the law in daily life, and the experts who taught the law
decisions.reason: The Pharisees were respected teachers among the people, and many of the scribes belonged to their party (5:30). Both groups were careful about whom they ate with.

decisions.choice: this man: said with scorn
decisions.reason: The leaders do not use Jesus' name. The same kind of phrase is used with scorn in 15:30, "this son of yours".

decisions.choice: receives and eats with: welcomes them as companions at the table
decisions.reason: To share a meal with someone was a sign of friendship and acceptance (5:29-30). The three parables that follow answer this complaint.

decisions.choice: teachers of the law (R); scribes (L, B)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the scribes did, as in 5:30.

decisions.choice: even shares meals with them
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out the force of the complaint, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: murmuraban
decisions.reason: "Murmurar" is the verb Spanish uses for Israel grumbling in the wilderness, so Literal and Readable keep the echo that meaning decision m1 points to; Balanced says "se quejaban entre sí", as the English says "complained among themselves".

decisions.choice: los escribas (L, B); los maestros de la ley (R)
decisions.reason: The experts who taught the law (meaning decision m2). Literal and Balanced keep the traditional title; Readable says what they did, as the English Readable does. The same through Luke.

decisions.choice: murmuraient (L, B); ont protesté (R)
decisions.reason: "Murmurer" is the word French uses for Israel's grumbling in the wilderness, so Literal and Balanced keep the possible echo (m1, uncertain); Readable says plainly that they protested.

decisions.choice: les scribes (L, B); les spécialistes de la Loi (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms, following the English "teachers of the law" at Readable; "la Loi" is capitalised for the Law of Moses.

decisions.choice: waandishi (L, B); walimu wa sheria (R)
decisions.reason: The experts who taught the law (meaning decision m2). Literal and Balanced keep the traditional title; Readable says what they did, as the English Readable does. The same through Luke.

decisions.choice: "lằm bằm" (L, B), "phàn nàn" (R); "thầy thông giáo" (L, B), "thầy dạy luật" (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:30 and 5:21: the old Bible word for Israel's grumbling, which the meaning decision hears here, and the settled terms for the scribes.

decisions.choice: "Người này" (L); "Gã này" (B); "Ông ta" (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:21: the meaning decision says "this man" is said with scorn, which Balanced carries in the slighting "gã".

source.text: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτοὺς τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην λέγων·

records.literal_gloss: He spoke then to them the parable this saying,

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke this parable to them, saying,
en.B: So Jesus put this parable to them:
en.R: So Jesus told them a story to teach them:

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les dijo esta parábola, diciendo:
es.B: Entonces Jesús les propuso esta parábola:
es.R: Entonces Jesús les contó una historia para enseñarles:

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur adressa cette parabole, en disant :
fr.B: Jésus leur proposa donc cette parabole :
fr.R: Alors Jésus leur a raconté une histoire pour les enseigner :

sw.L: Naye akawaambia mfano huu, akisema,
sw.B: Basi Yesu aliwapa mfano huu:
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Yesu aliwasimulia mfano ili kuwafundisha:

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ ngụ ngôn này rằng:
vi.B: Vậy Đức Giê-xu kể cho họ ngụ ngôn này:
vi.R: Vì vậy Đức Giê-xu kể cho họ một câu chuyện để dạy họ:

decisions.choice: parable: a story or comparison from everyday life that teaches about God and his kingdom
decisions.reason: As in 8:4 and 12:16. Luke speaks of one parable, though three stories follow: they make one answer to the complaint of 15:2.

decisions.choice: a story to teach them
decisions.reason: Readable says what a parable is, as in 12:16.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker after the Pharisees' words.

decisions.choice: parábola (L, B); una historia para enseñarles (R)
decisions.reason: A story from everyday life that teaches about God (meaning decision m1). Literal and Balanced keep "parábola"; Readable says "historia" where the English Readable says "story", as through Luke.

decisions.choice: mfano (every level)
decisions.reason: "Mfano" is both a comparison and a teaching story, so it serves at every level (meaning decision m1); Readable adds "aliwasimulia ... ili kuwafundisha" (told ... to teach them) to show it is a story, as the English Readable does.

source.text: Τίς ἄνθρωπος ἐξ ὑμῶν ἔχων ἑκατὸν πρόβατα καὶ ἀπολέσας ἐξ αὐτῶν ἓν οὐ καταλείπει τὰ ἐνενήκοντα ἐννέα ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ καὶ πορεύεται ἐπὶ τὸ ἀπολωλὸς ἕως εὕρῃ αὐτό;

records.literal_gloss: What man of you having a hundred sheep and having lost of them one not leaves the ninety nine in the open country and goes after the [one] having been lost until he finds it?

en.L: "What man of you, having a hundred sheep and having lost one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the open country and go after the lost one until he finds it?
en.B: "Which man among you, if he owned a hundred sheep and lost one of them, would not leave the ninety-nine out in the wild country and search for the lost one until he found it?
en.R: "If one of you had a hundred sheep and lost one of them, what would you do? You would leave the other ninety-nine in the open land where they graze. Then you would go and look for the lost sheep until you found it.

es.L: «¿Qué hombre de entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, teniendo cien ovejas y habiendo perdido una de ellas, no deja las noventa y nueve en el despoblado y va tras la perdida hasta que la encuentra?
es.B: «¿Quién de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, si tuviera cien ovejas y perdiera una, no dejaría las noventa y nueve en el monte para ir a buscar la extraviada hasta dar con ella?
es.R: «Si uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} tuviera cien ovejas y perdiera una, ¿qué haría? Dejaría las otras noventa y nueve en el campo, donde pastan. Luego saldría a buscar la oveja perdida, y no pararía hasta encontrarla.

fr.L: « Quel homme d’entre vous, ayant cent brebis et en ayant perdu une, ne laisse pas les quatre-vingt-dix-neuf dans la campagne déserte et ne va pas après celle qui est perdue, jusqu’à ce qu’il la trouve ?
fr.B: « Quel homme parmi vous, s’il avait cent brebis et qu’il en perdait une, ne laisserait pas les quatre-vingt-dix-neuf autres en pleine campagne pour partir à la recherche de celle qui s’est perdue, jusqu’à ce qu’il la retrouve ?
fr.R: « Supposons que vous ayez cent moutons et que vous en perdiez un. Que feriez-vous ? Vous laisseriez les quatre-vingt-dix-neuf autres dans les pâturages où ils broutent. Puis vous iriez chercher le mouton perdu jusqu’à ce que vous le retrouviez.

sw.L: "Ni mtu gani kati yenu mwenye kondoo mia moja ambaye, akimpoteza mmoja wao, hawaachi wale tisini na tisa nyikani na kumfuata yule aliyepotea mpaka ampate?
sw.B: "Ni nani kati yenu ambaye, kama angekuwa na kondoo mia moja na kumpoteza mmoja, asingewaacha wale tisini na tisa nyikani na kwenda kumtafuta aliyepotea hadi ampate?
sw.R: "Kama mmoja wenu angekuwa na kondoo mia moja, na mmoja wao akapotea, angefanya nini? Angewaacha wale tisini na tisa wengine mbugani wakila majani. Kisha angekwenda kumtafuta yule kondoo aliyepotea mpaka ampate.

vi.L: "Người nào trong các người có một trăm con chiên, mà mất một con, lại không để chín mươi chín con kia trong đồng hoang mà đi tìm con đã mất cho đến khi tìm được sao?
vi.B: "Ai trong các người có một trăm con chiên mà bị mất một con, lại không để chín mươi chín con kia ngoài đồng hoang mà đi tìm con chiên bị mất cho đến khi tìm được sao?
vi.R: "Giả sử một người trong các người có một trăm con chiên và bị mất một con. Người ấy sẽ làm gì? Người ấy sẽ để chín mươi chín con kia lại trên đồng cỏ, rồi đi tìm con chiên bị lạc cho đến khi tìm được.

decisions.choice: What man of you ... does not: a question that expects the answer that every one of them would
alternatives: a real question about what a shepherd might do
decisions.reason: The question invites the listeners to agree. Any of them would go after a lost animal; so they should understand why Jesus goes after lost people (15:2).

decisions.choice: the open country: wild grazing land, away from towns and fields
decisions.reason: The word means land where no one lives. In Judea it was rough hill country where flocks were taken to graze. The ninety-nine would be left with other shepherds or in a fold; the story does not stop to say.

decisions.choice: goes after the lost one: the shepherd who seeks the lost
decisions.reason: In Ezekiel 34:11-16 God himself promises to search for his scattered sheep and bring back the lost. Jesus says of himself that he came to seek and save the lost (19:10).

decisions.choice: lost: gone missing, strayed away
decisions.reason: The verb can mean destroy or perish (15:17), but with a sheep or a coin it means missing. The same word links all three parables (15:6, 9, 24, 32).

decisions.choice: a question to the listeners, then the answer in two statements, using "you"
alternatives: What man of you ... does not ...?
decisions.reason: Readable breaks up the long question and speaks to the listeners directly, as the Greek "of you" invites. Literal and Balanced keep the question.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs on to 15:10
decisions.reason: The sheep and the coin are one speech of Jesus. Luke's "He said" in 15:11 starts a new quotation.

decisions.choice: el despoblado (L); el monte (B); el campo, donde pastan (R)
decisions.reason: The place is wild grazing land away from towns (meaning decision m2), not sand desert, which "desierto" would suggest here. "Despoblado" is uninhabited land, and "monte" is the wild, uncultivated country where flocks graze.

decisions.choice: Si uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} tuviera ... ¿qué haría? Dejaría ...
decisions.reason: The English Readable turns to "you"; Spanish keeps the question to the listeners but, after "uno de ustedes", goes on naturally in the third person, through 15:6. Every plural "you" in this chapter takes the plural_you setting.

decisions.choice: brebis (L, B); moutons (R)
decisions.reason: "Brebis" is the word French has long used for the sheep of a flock and keeps the link with the shepherd imagery of Scripture (m3); Readable says "moutons", the everyday word, and speaks to the listeners with a generic "vous", as the English Readable does with "you".

decisions.choice: dans la campagne déserte (L); en pleine campagne (B); dans les pâturages où ils broutent (R)
decisions.reason: "Le désert" would suggest sand and no grass; the place is wild grazing land away from towns (m2).

decisions.choice: nyikani (L, B); mbugani wakila majani (R)
decisions.reason: Wild grazing land away from towns (meaning decision m2). "Nyika" is the uninhabited bush, as through Luke; Readable names the grassland where the sheep graze, as the English Readable does, rather than "jangwa", which would suggest a place without grass.

decisions.choice: Kama mmoja wenu angekuwa ... angefanya nini? Angewaacha ...
decisions.reason: The English Readable turns to "you"; Swahili keeps the question to the listeners but, after "mmoja wenu", goes on in the third person, through 15:6.

decisions.choice: Jesus speaks to the Pharisees and scribes as "các người" through 15:10
decisions.reason: The style guide's form for opponents, as in 5:22.

decisions.choice: the shepherd is "người ấy" (R) where the English Readable says "you", through 15:6
decisions.reason: The Greek asks "what man of you" and then speaks of that man; Vietnamese has no neutral singular "you" for a group, so Readable keeps the third person while still setting out the case and the answer, as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ εὑρὼν ἐπιτίθησιν ἐπὶ τοὺς ὤμους αὐτοῦ χαίρων, καὶ ἐλθὼν εἰς τὸν οἶκον συγκαλεῖ τοὺς φίλους καὶ τοὺς γείτονας, λέγων αὐτοῖς· Συγχάρητέ μοι ὅτι εὗρον τὸ πρόβατόν μου τὸ ἀπολωλός.

records.literal_gloss: And having found [it] he lays [it] on the shoulders of him rejoicing, \v 6 and having come to the house he calls together the friends and the neighbors saying to them, Rejoice with me, for I have found the sheep of me the [one] having been lost.

en.L: And having found [it], he lays [it] on his shoulders, rejoicing, \v 6 and coming to the house, he calls together the friends and the neighbors, saying to them, 'Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep that was lost.'
en.B: And when he finds it, he hoists it onto his shoulders, delighted. \v 6 Back at home, he invites his friends and neighbors over. 'Celebrate with me,' he tells them, 'because the sheep I lost has been found.'
en.R: When you found it, you would be so glad that you would lift it up onto your shoulders and carry it. \v 6 You would go home and get your friends and neighbors together. You would say to them, 'Be glad with me! I have found my lost sheep!'

es.L: Y habiendo encontrado[la], [la] pone sobre sus hombros, alegre, \v 6 y llegando a la casa, convoca a los amigos y a los vecinos, diciéndoles: “{{plural_you:Alégrense|Alegraos}} conmigo, porque encontré mi oveja, la que se había perdido”.
es.B: Y cuando la encuentra, se la carga a los hombros, feliz. \v 6 De vuelta en casa, invita a sus amigos y vecinos. “{{plural_you:Celebren|Celebrad}} conmigo —les dice—, porque la oveja que había perdido ha aparecido”.
es.R: Cuando la encontrara, estaría tan contento que la levantaría sobre sus hombros y la llevaría. \v 6 Se iría a casa y reuniría a sus amigos y vecinos. Les diría: “¡{{plural_you:Alégrense|Alegraos}} conmigo! ¡Encontré mi oveja perdida!”.

fr.L: Et l’ayant trouvée, il [la] met sur ses épaules, tout joyeux, \v 6 et, arrivé à la maison, il réunit les amis et les voisins, leur disant : “Réjouissez-vous avec moi, car j’ai trouvé ma brebis qui était perdue.”
fr.B: Quand il l’a retrouvée, il la charge sur ses épaules, plein de joie. \v 6 De retour chez lui, il invite ses amis et ses voisins. “Partagez ma joie, leur dit-il : la brebis que j’avais perdue, je l’ai retrouvée.”
fr.R: Quand vous l’auriez retrouvé, vous seriez si content que vous le prendriez sur vos épaules pour le porter. \v 6 Vous rentreriez chez vous et vous réuniriez vos amis et vos voisins. Vous leur diriez : “Réjouissez-vous avec moi ! J’ai retrouvé mon mouton perdu !”

sw.L: Na akimpata, anamweka mabegani mwake akishangilia, \v 6 na akiingia nyumbani, anawaita pamoja marafiki na majirani, akiwaambia, 'Shangilieni pamoja nami, kwa maana nimempata kondoo wangu yule aliyepotea.'
sw.B: Akimpata, anambeba mabegani kwa furaha. \v 6 Akirudi nyumbani, anawaalika marafiki na majirani zake. Anawaambia, 'Shereheni pamoja nami, kwa sababu kondoo niliyempoteza amepatikana.'
sw.R: Akimpata, angefurahi sana hata angembeba mabegani mwake. \v 6 Angerudi nyumbani na kuwaita marafiki na majirani zake. Angewaambia, 'Furahini pamoja nami! Nimempata kondoo wangu aliyepotea!'

vi.L: Và khi tìm được, người ấy vác [nó] lên vai mình, vui mừng; \v 6 và về đến nhà, người ấy gọi bạn bè và láng giềng lại, nói với họ: 'Hãy vui mừng với tôi, vì tôi đã tìm được con chiên của tôi đã bị mất.'
vi.B: Khi tìm được, người ấy vui mừng vác nó lên vai. \v 6 Về đến nhà, người ấy mời bạn bè và láng giềng đến và nói với họ: 'Hãy chung vui với tôi, vì con chiên bị mất của tôi đã tìm được rồi!'
vi.R: Khi tìm được, người ấy vui mừng lắm, nhấc nó lên vai và vác về. \v 6 Về đến nhà, người ấy gọi bạn bè và hàng xóm đến. Người ấy nói với họ: 'Hãy vui với tôi! Tôi đã tìm được con chiên bị lạc của tôi rồi!'

decisions.choice: lays it on his shoulders: the usual way to carry a sheep, with its legs held at the front
decisions.reason: A tired or frightened sheep may not follow, so the shepherd carries it the whole way home. He does it gladly, not as a burden.

decisions.choice: rejoice with me: share my joy
decisions.reason: The verb means to rejoice together. The finder wants others to share the gladness, as the father does in 15:23-24 and as the elder son refuses to do (15:28).

decisions.choice: that was lost: the sheep that had been lost
decisions.reason: The participle describes the sheep's state before it was found.

decisions.choice: because the sheep I lost has been found
alternatives: for I have found my sheep that was lost
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the lost sheep first, which reads naturally and keeps the meaning.

decisions.choice: you would be so glad
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the "you" of 15:4 and makes the man's gladness its own clause.

decisions.choice: Jesus' words in « », the words of the people in his stories in “ ”, and words they quote or plan to say in ‘ ’
alternatives: the English pattern of double and single marks
decisions.reason: French typography nests « », then “ ”, then ‘ ’. The quotation that opened in 15:4 runs on to 15:10, as in the English.

decisions.choice: "vác", "gọi" with no past marker (L)
decisions.reason: The style guide keeps the historic present at Literal by leaving out "đã"; the same in 15:8-9.

source.text: λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὕτως χαρὰ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ἔσται ἐπὶ ἑνὶ ἁμαρτωλῷ μετανοοῦντι ἢ ἐπὶ ἐνενήκοντα ἐννέα δικαίοις οἵτινες οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν μετανοίας.

records.literal_gloss: I say to you that in the same way joy in the heaven there will be over one sinner repenting rather than over ninety nine righteous ones who no need have of repentance.

en.L: I tell you that in the same way there will be joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, [more] than over ninety-nine righteous [people] who have no need of repentance.
en.B: In the same way, I tell you, one sinner who repents will bring more joy in heaven than ninety-nine righteous people who have no need to repent.
en.R: I tell you, it is the same in heaven. When one sinner turns away from sin and comes back to God, there is joy in heaven. There is more joy over that one person than over ninety-nine people who are already right with God and do not need to turn back.

es.L: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo que así habrá alegría en el cielo por un pecador que se arrepiente, [más] que por noventa y nueve justos que no tienen necesidad de arrepentimiento.
es.B: Del mismo modo, {{plural_you:les|os}} digo, un solo pecador que se arrepiente causará en el cielo más alegría que noventa y nueve justos que no necesitan arrepentirse.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo que en el cielo pasa lo mismo. Cuando un pecador se aparta del pecado y vuelve a Dios, hay alegría en el cielo. Hay más alegría por esa persona que por noventa y nueve que ya están bien con Dios y no necesitan regresar.

fr.L: Je vous dis que de même il y aura de la joie dans le ciel pour un seul pécheur qui se repent, [plus] que pour quatre-vingt-dix-neuf justes qui n’ont pas besoin de repentance.
fr.B: De la même manière, je vous le dis, un seul pécheur qui se repent causera plus de joie dans le ciel que quatre-vingt-dix-neuf justes qui n’ont pas besoin de se repentir.
fr.R: Je vous le dis, c’est la même chose au ciel. Quand un seul pécheur se détourne du mal et revient vers Dieu, il y a de la joie au ciel. Il y a plus de joie pour cette seule personne que pour quatre-vingt-dix-neuf personnes qui sont déjà en règle avec Dieu et qui n’ont pas besoin de changer de vie.

sw.L: Nawaambia kwamba hivyo ndivyo itakavyokuwa furaha mbinguni juu ya mwenye dhambi mmoja anayetubu, [zaidi] kuliko juu ya wenye haki tisini na tisa ambao hawana haja ya toba.
sw.B: Vivyo hivyo, nawaambia, mwenye dhambi mmoja anayetubu ataleta furaha kubwa zaidi mbinguni kuliko wenye haki tisini na tisa ambao hawana haja ya kutubu.
sw.R: Nawaambia, ndivyo ilivyo mbinguni. Mwenye dhambi mmoja anapoacha dhambi zake na kumrudia Mungu, kunakuwa na furaha mbinguni. Furaha juu ya mtu huyo mmoja ni kubwa kuliko furaha juu ya watu tisini na tisa ambao tayari wako sawa na Mungu, wasiohitaji kumrudia.

vi.L: Ta nói với các người rằng cũng như vậy, trên trời sẽ có niềm vui về một người tội lỗi ăn năn, [hơn] là về chín mươi chín người công chính không cần đến sự ăn năn.
vi.B: Ta nói với các người, cũng vậy, trên trời sẽ vui mừng về một người tội lỗi ăn năn hơn là về chín mươi chín người công chính không cần phải ăn năn.
vi.R: Ta nói cho các người biết, ở trên trời cũng giống như vậy. Khi một người tội lỗi từ bỏ tội lỗi và quay về với Đức Chúa Trời, thì trên trời có niềm vui. Trên trời vui mừng về một người ấy nhiều hơn là về chín mươi chín người đã sống đúng với Đức Chúa Trời và không cần phải quay về.

decisions.choice: in heaven: with God, who lives in heaven
decisions.reason: Jewish speech often said "heaven" in place of God's name, out of reverence (15:18). The joy in heaven is God's own joy.

decisions.choice: rather than: more ... than, a comparison
alternatives: instead of: there is no joy over the ninety-nine
decisions.reason: The word means "than" after a comparison that is left unsaid. The point is the special gladness over the one who comes back, not that God takes no pleasure in the others.

decisions.choice: repents; repentance: turning from sin back to God
decisions.reason: The same words John and Jesus used (3:3; 5:32). In the parable the sheep is found by the shepherd; in the saying the sinner turns back. Both are true of what happens when Jesus welcomes sinners.

decisions.choice: righteous people who have no need of repentance: people who keep the law, or who think they do
alternatives: people who have no sin at all
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks in his hearers' own terms, as in 5:32. Luke tells of some who trusted that they were righteous (18:9). Whether there is irony here is left for the listeners to see.

decisions.choice: [more]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the comparison the Greek leaves implied.

decisions.choice: turns away from sin and comes back to God; people who are already right with God; do not need to turn back
decisions.reason: Readable explains both words, as in 5:32.

decisions.choice: se arrepiente, arrepentimiento (L, B); se aparta del pecado y vuelve a Dios (R)
decisions.reason: "Arrepentirse" is the word for repentance through Luke (meaning decision m3); Readable says what it is, turning from sin back to God, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: se repentir, la repentance, justes (L, B); se détourne du mal et revient vers Dieu, en règle avec Dieu, changer de vie (R)
alternatives: changer de vie at every level
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms: Literal and Balanced keep the key words, and Readable explains them as the English Readable does (m3, m4).

decisions.choice: anayetubu, toba (L, B); anapoacha dhambi zake na kumrudia Mungu (R)
decisions.reason: "Kutubu" and "toba" are the words for repentance through Luke (meaning decision m3); Readable says what it is, turning from sin back to God, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "ăn năn", "sự ăn năn" (L, B); "từ bỏ tội lỗi và quay về với Đức Chúa Trời" (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:32 and 13:3; kept in 15:10.

source.text: Ἢ τίς γυνὴ δραχμὰς ἔχουσα δέκα, ἐὰν ἀπολέσῃ δραχμὴν μίαν, οὐχὶ ἅπτει λύχνον καὶ σαροῖ τὴν οἰκίαν καὶ ζητεῖ ἐπιμελῶς ἕως οὗ εὕρῃ;

records.literal_gloss: Or what woman drachmas having ten, if she should lose drachma one, not lights a lamp and sweeps the house and seeks carefully until that she finds [it]?

en.L: Or what woman, having ten drachmas, if she loses one drachma, does not light a lamp and sweep the house and search carefully until she finds [it]?
en.B: Or what woman with ten silver coins, if she lost one of them, would not light a lamp, sweep out her house and hunt for it carefully until she found it?
en.R: Or think about a woman who has ten silver coins. If she loses one of them, she will light a lamp and sweep the whole house. She will look carefully everywhere until she finds it.

es.L: ¿O qué mujer, teniendo diez dracmas, si llegara a perder una sola dracma, no prende una lámpara y barre la casa y busca cuidadosamente hasta hallar[la]?
es.B: ¿O qué mujer con diez monedas de plata, si perdiera una, no encendería una lámpara, barrería bien la casa y la buscaría con esmero hasta dar con ella?
es.R: O {{plural_you:piensen|pensad}} en una mujer que tiene diez monedas de plata. Si pierde una, enciende una lámpara y barre toda la casa. Busca con cuidado por todas partes hasta que la encuentra.

fr.L: Ou quelle femme, ayant dix drachmes, si elle perd une drachme, n’allume pas une lampe, ne balaie pas la maison et ne cherche pas avec soin jusqu’à ce qu’elle [la] trouve ?
fr.B: Ou bien quelle femme, si elle avait dix pièces d’argent et qu’elle en perdait une, n’allumerait pas une lampe, ne balaierait pas sa maison et ne la chercherait pas avec soin jusqu’à ce qu’elle la retrouve ?
fr.R: Ou bien pensez à une femme qui a dix pièces d’argent. Si elle en perd une, elle va allumer une lampe et balayer toute la maison. Elle va chercher partout avec soin jusqu’à ce qu’elle la retrouve.

sw.L: Au ni mwanamke gani mwenye drakma kumi, akipoteza drakma moja, asiyewasha taa na kufagia nyumba na kutafuta kwa uangalifu mpaka aipate?
sw.B: Au ni mwanamke gani ambaye, akiwa na sarafu kumi za fedha na kupoteza moja, asingewasha taa, akaifagia nyumba yake na kuitafuta kwa uangalifu mpaka aipate?
sw.R: Au fikirini kuhusu mwanamke mwenye sarafu kumi za fedha. Akipoteza moja, atawasha taa na kufagia nyumba yote. Atatafuta kwa uangalifu kila mahali mpaka aipate.

vi.L: Hoặc người phụ nữ nào có mười đồng đơ-rắc-ma, nếu đánh mất một đồng, lại không thắp đèn, quét nhà và tìm kiếm kỹ lưỡng cho đến khi tìm được sao?
vi.B: Hoặc có người phụ nữ nào có mười đồng bạc, nếu đánh mất một đồng, lại không thắp đèn, quét nhà và tìm kỹ cho đến khi tìm được sao?
vi.R: Hoặc hãy nghĩ đến một người phụ nữ có mười đồng bạc. Nếu bà đánh mất một đồng, bà sẽ thắp đèn và quét khắp nhà. Bà sẽ tìm kỹ mọi nơi cho đến khi tìm được.

decisions.choice: drachma: a Greek silver coin worth about a day's wages
decisions.reason: A drachma was worth about the same as a Roman denarius, the day's wage of a laborer (Matthew 20:2). Ten of them were a large sum for a poor household, perhaps her savings, so the loss of one was serious.

decisions.choice: lights a lamp and sweeps the house: searching a dark house with a dirt or stone floor
decisions.reason: Village houses had small windows and floors of beaten earth or stone. A small coin could be found only with a lamp and a broom.

decisions.choice: Or what woman ... does not: a second question that expects the answer that any woman would
decisions.reason: The second parable has the same shape as the first (15:4). A woman stands beside the shepherd as a picture of God seeking the lost.

decisions.choice: silver coins (B, R); drachmas (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the coin's name. Balanced and Readable say what kind of coin it was, as Readable does with the denarius in 10:35; the meaning decision gives its value.

decisions.choice: two statements
decisions.reason: Readable gives the answer to the question, as in 15:4.

decisions.choice: drakma (L); sarafu za fedha (B, R)
decisions.reason: A Greek silver coin worth about a day's wages (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the coin's name; Balanced and Readable say "silver coins", as the English does. "Shilingi" would put a modern currency into the story.

decisions.choice: "đồng đơ-rắc-ma" (L); "đồng bạc" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The coin's name as in Matthew 17:24 at Literal; Balanced and Readable say what it was, a silver coin, as the English does. The English has no Measures setting here, so neither does the Vietnamese.

source.text: καὶ εὑροῦσα συγκαλεῖ τὰς φίλας καὶ γείτονας λέγουσα· Συγχάρητέ μοι ὅτι εὗρον τὴν δραχμὴν ἣν ἀπώλεσα.

records.literal_gloss: And having found [it] she calls together the friends and neighbors saying, Rejoice with me, for I have found the drachma that I lost.

en.L: And having found [it], she calls together the friends and neighbors, saying, 'Rejoice with me, for I have found the drachma that I lost.'
en.B: When she finds it, she gathers her friends and neighbors. 'Be glad with me,' she says, 'for the coin I had lost is found.'
en.R: When she finds it, she asks her friends and neighbors to come over. She says to them, 'Be happy with me! I found the coin I lost!'

es.L: Y habiendo hallado[la], convoca a las amigas y vecinas, diciendo: “{{plural_you:Alégrense|Alegraos}} conmigo, porque hallé la dracma que perdí”.
es.B: Cuando la encuentra, reúne a sus amigas y vecinas. “{{plural_you:Alégrense|Alegraos}} conmigo —les dice—, porque ha aparecido la moneda que había perdido”.
es.R: Cuando la encuentra, invita a sus amigas y vecinas a su casa. Les dice: “¡{{plural_you:Alégrense|Alegraos}} conmigo! ¡Encontré la moneda que había perdido!”.

fr.L: Et l’ayant trouvée, elle réunit les amies et les voisines, disant : “Réjouissez-vous avec moi, car j’ai trouvé la drachme que j’avais perdue.”
fr.B: Quand elle l’a retrouvée, elle rassemble ses amies et ses voisines. “Partagez ma joie, leur dit-elle : la pièce que j’avais perdue est retrouvée.”
fr.R: Quand elle la retrouve, elle invite ses amies et ses voisines à venir chez elle. Elle leur dit : “Réjouissez-vous avec moi ! J’ai retrouvé la pièce que j’avais perdue !”

sw.L: Na akiipata, anawaita pamoja rafiki zake na majirani, akisema, 'Shangilieni pamoja nami, kwa maana nimeipata drakma niliyoipoteza.'
sw.B: Anapoipata, anawakusanya rafiki zake na majirani. Anawaambia, 'Furahini pamoja nami, kwa sababu ile sarafu niliyokuwa nimeipoteza imepatikana.'
sw.R: Akiipata, anawaita rafiki zake na majirani waje kwake. Anawaambia, 'Furahini pamoja nami! Nimeipata sarafu niliyoipoteza!'

vi.L: Và khi tìm được, bà gọi các bạn và láng giềng lại, nói: 'Hãy vui mừng với tôi, vì tôi đã tìm được đồng đơ-rắc-ma tôi đã đánh mất.'
vi.B: Khi tìm được rồi, bà gọi bạn bè và láng giềng đến và nói: 'Hãy chung vui với tôi, vì đồng bạc tôi đánh mất đã tìm được rồi!'
vi.R: Khi tìm được, bà mời bạn bè và hàng xóm đến. Bà nói với họ: 'Hãy vui với tôi! Tôi đã tìm được đồng bạc tôi đánh mất rồi!'

decisions.choice: rejoice with me: share my joy
decisions.reason: As in 15:6. The friends here are women, as the Greek forms show.

decisions.choice: that I lost: she owns the loss
decisions.reason: The shepherd speaks of the sheep that was lost; the woman says plainly that she lost the coin. Either way, the owner goes looking.

decisions.choice: coin (B, R); drachma (L)
decisions.reason: As in 15:8.

decisions.choice: las amigas y vecinas
decisions.reason: The Greek words are feminine: she calls together her women friends and neighbours. Spanish can show this, as English cannot.

decisions.choice: les amies et les voisines
decisions.reason: The Greek nouns are feminine, so the woman calls her women friends and neighbours; French must mark the gender and can follow the Greek, where English "friends and neighbors" need not choose.

source.text: οὕτως, λέγω ὑμῖν, γίνεται χαρὰ ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀγγέλων τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπὶ ἑνὶ ἁμαρτωλῷ μετανοοῦντι.

records.literal_gloss: Thus I say to you, there is joy before the angels of the God over one sinner repenting.

en.L: Thus, I tell you, there is joy before the angels of God over one sinner who repents."
en.B: So it is, I tell you: when one sinner repents, there is joy before the angels of God."
en.R: I tell you, it is the same with God. When just one sinner turns away from sin and comes back to God, there is joy in the presence of God's angels."

es.L: Así, {{plural_you:les|os}} digo, surge alegría delante de los ángeles de Dios por un pecador que se arrepiente».
es.B: Así es, {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: cuando un pecador se arrepiente, hay alegría ante los ángeles de Dios».
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo que con Dios pasa lo mismo. Cuando un solo pecador se aparta del pecado y vuelve a Dios, hay alegría en presencia de los ángeles de Dios».

fr.L: Ainsi, je vous le dis, il y a de la joie devant les anges de Dieu pour un seul pécheur qui se repent. »
fr.B: C’est ainsi, je vous le dis : quand un seul pécheur se repent, il y a de la joie devant les anges de Dieu. »
fr.R: Je vous le dis, c’est la même chose pour Dieu. Quand un seul pécheur se détourne du mal et revient vers Dieu, il y a de la joie devant les anges de Dieu. »

sw.L: Hivyo, nawaambia, kunakuwa na furaha mbele ya malaika wa Mungu juu ya mwenye dhambi mmoja anayetubu."
sw.B: Ndivyo ilivyo, nawaambia: mwenye dhambi mmoja anapotubu, furaha inakuwako mbele ya malaika wa Mungu."
sw.R: Nawaambia, ndivyo ilivyo kwa Mungu. Hata mwenye dhambi mmoja tu anapoacha dhambi zake na kumrudia Mungu, kunakuwa na furaha mbele ya malaika wa Mungu."

vi.L: Cũng vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các người, có niềm vui trước mặt các thiên sứ của Đức Chúa Trời về một người tội lỗi ăn năn."
vi.B: Ta nói với các người, cũng thế, khi một người tội lỗi ăn năn, thì có niềm vui trước mặt các thiên sứ của Đức Chúa Trời."
vi.R: Ta nói cho các người biết, với Đức Chúa Trời cũng giống như vậy. Khi chỉ một người tội lỗi từ bỏ tội lỗi và quay về với Đức Chúa Trời, thì có niềm vui trước mặt các thiên sứ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}."

decisions.choice: joy before the angels of God: joy in God's presence, where the angels stand
alternatives: joy felt only by the angels
decisions.reason: "Before" means in the presence of. It is a reverent way of speaking about God's own joy, which his angels see and share (compare 15:7, "in heaven"; 12:8-9).

decisions.choice: repents: turns from sin back to God
decisions.reason: As in 15:7.

decisions.choice: turns away from sin and comes back to God
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word, as in 15:7.

decisions.choice: the quotation closes here
decisions.reason: Luke's own words in 15:11 interrupt Jesus' speech, so the quotation closes and opens again, as at 6:39.

source.text: Εἶπεν δέ· Ἄνθρωπός τις εἶχεν δύο υἱούς.

records.literal_gloss: He said then, A man certain had two sons.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "A certain man had two sons.
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "A man had two sons.
en.R: Then Jesus told another story: "There was once a man who had two sons.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} dijo: «Cierto hombre tenía dos hijos.
es.B: Luego dijo: «Un hombre tenía dos hijos.
es.R: Luego Jesús contó otra historia: «Había una vez un hombre que tenía dos hijos.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Un certain homme avait deux fils.
fr.B: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Un homme avait deux fils.
fr.R: Ensuite, Jésus a raconté une autre histoire : « Il y avait un homme qui avait deux fils.

sw.L: Naye akasema, "Mtu fulani alikuwa na wana wawili.
sw.B: Kisha akasema, "Palikuwa na mtu mwenye wana wawili.
sw.R: Kisha Yesu alisimulia mfano mwingine: "Hapo zamani palikuwa na mtu mmoja aliyekuwa na wana wawili wa kiume.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói: "Một người kia có hai con trai.
vi.B: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói tiếp: "Có một người có hai con trai.
vi.R: Rồi Đức Giê-xu kể một câu chuyện khác: "Ngày xưa có một người có hai con trai.

decisions.choice: a man had two sons: the story is about both sons and their father
alternatives: a story about the younger son alone
decisions.reason: The opening words name two sons. The second half of the story (15:25-32) is about the elder son, who answers to the grumbling of 15:2.

decisions.choice: a man: a figure in a parable
decisions.reason: The father's welcome pictures God's welcome of sinners, but he is a character in a story, and the text speaks of him as a man.

decisions.choice: Jesus told another story
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker and shows that a new story begins.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs on to 15:32; the speakers' words are in single quotation marks, and words they plan or quote in double ones
alternatives: a new quotation for each speaker
decisions.reason: The story is one speech of Jesus with the speakers' words inside it.

decisions.choice: « » for Jesus, “ ” for the speakers in the story, ‘ ’ for words they plan or quote
decisions.reason: The quotation opens here and runs on to 15:32 (as the English decision says). Spanish uses its own three levels of quotation marks, so the son's planned words in 15:18-19 are in ‘ ’.

decisions.choice: the parable of 15:11-32 in the passé composé at every level ("le plus jeune a dit", "il est parti"), with the imperfect for settings
alternatives: the passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: The story is Jesus' speech, and French speech tells past events in the passé composé, as the style guide asks for parables (Mark 4, 12). Luke's own narration around it (15:11a) keeps the passé simple at Literal and Balanced.

source.text: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ νεώτερος αὐτῶν τῷ πατρί· Πάτερ, δός μοι τὸ ἐπιβάλλον μέρος τῆς οὐσίας· ὁ δὲ διεῖλεν αὐτοῖς τὸν βίον.

records.literal_gloss: And said the younger of them to the father, Father, give me the falling [to me] portion of the property. And he divided between them the living.

en.L: And the younger of them said to the father, 'Father, give me the portion of the property that falls [to me].' And he divided the living between them.
en.B: The younger son said to his father, 'Father, let me have the part of the estate that will come to me.' So the father split what he had between the two of them.
en.R: The younger son said to his father, 'Father, give me now the part of your property that I will get one day.' So the father divided everything he owned between his two sons.

es.L: Y dijo el menor de ellos al padre: “Padre, dame la porción de la hacienda que [me] toca”. Y él les dividió el sustento.
es.B: El hijo menor le dijo a su padre: “Padre, dame la parte del patrimonio que me ha de tocar”. Así que el padre repartió entre los dos lo que tenía.
es.R: El hijo menor le dijo a su padre: “Padre, dame ahora la parte de tus bienes que algún día me va a tocar”. Entonces el padre dividió todo lo que tenía entre sus dos hijos.

fr.L: Et le plus jeune d’entre eux a dit au père : “Père, donne-moi la part des biens qui [me] revient.” Et il a partagé entre eux ce dont il vivait.
fr.B: Le plus jeune a dit à son père : “Père, donne-moi la part du patrimoine qui doit me revenir.” Alors le père a partagé entre eux deux ce qu’il possédait.
fr.R: Le plus jeune fils a dit à son père : “Père, donne-moi dès maintenant la part de tes biens que je recevrai un jour.” Alors le père a partagé tout ce qu’il possédait entre ses deux fils.

sw.L: Na yule mdogo wao akamwambia baba, 'Baba, nipe fungu la mali linaloniangukia.' Naye akawagawanyia riziki.
sw.B: Yule mwana mdogo alimwambia baba yake, 'Baba, nipe fungu la urithi litakalonihusu.' Basi baba akawagawia wote wawili alichokuwa nacho.
sw.R: Mwana mdogo alimwambia baba yake, 'Baba, nipe sasa sehemu ya mali yako ambayo ningeipata siku moja.' Basi baba aligawanya kila kitu alichokuwa nacho kati ya wanawe wawili.

vi.L: Và người nhỏ hơn trong hai người nói với cha: 'Thưa cha, xin cho con phần tài sản thuộc về con.' Và người cha chia của cải cho họ.
vi.B: Người con út thưa với cha: 'Thưa cha, xin cha cho con phần gia tài con sẽ được hưởng.' Vậy người cha chia của cải mình cho hai con.
vi.R: Người con út nói với cha: 'Thưa cha, xin cha cho con ngay bây giờ phần tài sản mà sau này con sẽ được hưởng.' Vậy người cha chia hết tài sản mình cho hai con trai.

decisions.choice: give me the portion that falls to me: his share of the inheritance, asked for while his father is still alive
decisions.reason: A father could divide his property while he lived, but a son had no right to demand it. Under the law the elder son received a double share (Deuteronomy 21:17), so the younger son's share would be a third. The request treats the father as if he were already gone.

decisions.choice: the living: the property a family lives on
decisions.reason: The word means life, and also the means of life: the land and goods that support a household (21:4). The father divides it between both sons (15:31).

decisions.choice: property: what a person owns
decisions.reason: A different word from "living" at the end of the verse, with much the same meaning.

decisions.choice: now ... that I will get one day
decisions.reason: Readable shows that he asked for his inheritance early, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: riziki
decisions.reason: "The living" is the property a family lives on (meaning decision m2). "Riziki" is a person's livelihood, the means to live; "maisha" would be read as his life itself.

decisions.choice: the sons say "Thưa cha", "cha" for "you" and "con" for themselves; the father says "cha" and "con"; "cha" in lowercase
decisions.reason: The ordinary words between a Vietnamese father and his grown sons, kept through the parable. The father is a man in a story, so "cha" is not capitalised as it is for God the Father.

source.text: καὶ μετ’ οὐ πολλὰς ἡμέρας συναγαγὼν πάντα ὁ νεώτερος υἱὸς ἀπεδήμησεν εἰς χώραν μακράν, καὶ ἐκεῖ διεσκόρπισεν τὴν οὐσίαν αὐτοῦ ζῶν ἀσώτως.

records.literal_gloss: And after not many days having gathered together all the younger son went away into a country distant, and there he wasted the property of him living prodigally.

en.L: And not many days later, having gathered everything together, the younger son went away to a distant country, and there he scattered his property, living wastefully.
en.B: Only a few days later the younger son packed up everything he owned and traveled to a far country, where he threw his property away on a reckless way of life.
en.R: Soon after that, the younger son packed up everything he had and went to a country far away. There he wasted all his money. He lived a reckless life.

es.L: Y no muchos días después, habiéndolo juntado todo, el hijo menor se fue a un país lejano, y allí desperdigó su hacienda viviendo disolutamente.
es.B: Al cabo de pocos días, el hijo menor reunió todo lo suyo y partió a una tierra lejana, y allí despilfarró sus bienes en una vida sin control.
es.R: Poco tiempo después, el hijo menor empacó todo lo que tenía y se fue a un país muy lejano. Allí malgastó todo su dinero. Llevaba una vida alocada.

fr.L: Et peu de jours après, ayant tout rassemblé, le plus jeune fils est parti pour un pays lointain, et là il a dissipé son bien en vivant sans retenue.
fr.B: Quelques jours plus tard, le plus jeune fils a rassemblé tout ce qu’il avait et il est parti pour un pays lointain, où il a gaspillé son bien en menant une vie de désordre.
fr.R: Peu de temps après, le plus jeune fils a emporté tout ce qu’il avait et il est parti dans un pays très loin. Là-bas, il a dépensé tout son argent. Il a vécu n’importe comment.

sw.L: Na baada ya siku zisizo nyingi, akiisha kukusanya vyote, yule mwana mdogo alisafiri kwenda nchi ya mbali, na huko akaitawanya mali yake, akiishi kwa ufujaji.
sw.B: Siku chache baadaye yule mwana mdogo alifunga virago vyake vyote, akaenda nchi ya mbali; huko akaifuja mali yake kwa maisha ya anasa ovyo.
sw.R: Baada ya muda mfupi, mwana mdogo alifunga vitu vyake vyote, akaenda nchi iliyo mbali sana. Huko alipoteza fedha zake zote. Aliishi bila kujali.

vi.L: Và không bao nhiêu ngày sau, người con trai út gom góp mọi thứ, đi sang một xứ xa, và tại đó phung phí tài sản mình, sống phóng đãng.
vi.B: Chỉ ít ngày sau, người con út thu gom mọi thứ mình có và đi đến một xứ xa. Ở đó anh phung phí tài sản mình trong một lối sống trác táng.
vi.R: Ít lâu sau, người con út gom hết mọi thứ mình có và đi đến một xứ rất xa. Ở đó anh tiêu xài phung phí hết tiền bạc. Anh sống một cuộc đời buông thả.

decisions.choice: having gathered everything together: collected all he had, perhaps by turning it into money
decisions.reason: The verb can be used of turning property into cash. He took everything with him, so that nothing was left behind.

decisions.choice: scattered: wasted, threw away
decisions.reason: The verb means to scatter, as grain is scattered. It is used of the manager who wastes his master's goods (16:1).

decisions.choice: living wastefully: without care or self-control
decisions.reason: The word describes a life with no restraint, spending without thought. The text does not say here how he spent it; the elder brother later claims it was on prostitutes (15:30).

decisions.choice: a distant country: a land of Gentiles, far from his family and his people
decisions.reason: The pigs of 15:15 show that he was among people who did not keep the law of Moses.

decisions.choice: wasted all his money
decisions.reason: Readable uses everyday words for what he did.

decisions.choice: il a dissipé son bien (L)
decisions.reason: "Dissiper" first means to scatter and is the usual French word for squandering a fortune, so Literal keeps both the image and the sense (m2).

decisions.choice: the narrator calls the sons "anh"
decisions.reason: A neutral word for a young grown man; "hắn" would judge the younger son before the story does.

source.text: δαπανήσαντος δὲ αὐτοῦ πάντα ἐγένετο λιμὸς ἰσχυρὰ κατὰ τὴν χώραν ἐκείνην, καὶ αὐτὸς ἤρξατο ὑστερεῖσθαι.

records.literal_gloss: Having spent however of him all, there arose a famine severe throughout the country that, and he began to be in need.

en.L: And when he had spent everything, a severe famine came over that country, and he began to be in need.
en.B: When he had used up everything, a terrible famine struck that whole land, and he began to go without.
en.R: When all his money was gone, a bad famine came to that country. There was very little food, and he did not have what he needed.

es.L: Y cuando él lo hubo gastado todo, vino una hambruna severa por toda aquella región, y él empezó a padecer necesidad.
es.B: Cuando ya lo había gastado todo, una terrible hambruna azotó aquella tierra, y él comenzó a pasar privaciones.
es.R: Cuando se le acabó todo el dinero, hubo una gran hambruna en aquel país. Había muy poca comida, y a él le faltaba lo necesario.

fr.L: Et quand il a eu tout dépensé, une forte famine est survenue dans ce pays-là, et lui a commencé à être dans le besoin.
fr.B: Quand il n’a plus rien eu, une terrible famine a frappé tout ce pays, et il a commencé à manquer de tout.
fr.R: Quand il n’a plus eu d’argent, une grande famine est arrivée dans ce pays. Il y avait très peu à manger, et il n’avait plus ce qu’il lui fallait pour vivre.

sw.L: Na baada ya yeye kutumia kila kitu, njaa kali iliingia katika nchi ile yote, naye akaanza kupungukiwa.
sw.B: Alipokuwa amemaliza kila kitu, njaa kubwa ilienea katika nchi ile yote, akaanza kukosa mahitaji.
sw.R: Fedha zake zote zilipokwisha, njaa kali ilitokea katika nchi ile. Chakula kilikuwa kidogo sana, naye hakuwa na alichohitaji.

vi.L: Khi anh đã tiêu hết mọi thứ, thì xảy ra một nạn đói lớn trong xứ ấy, và anh bắt đầu lâm vào cảnh thiếu thốn.
vi.B: Khi anh đã tiêu sạch mọi thứ, thì một nạn đói khủng khiếp xảy ra khắp xứ ấy, và anh bắt đầu lâm vào cảnh túng thiếu.
vi.R: Khi anh tiêu hết tiền, thì có một nạn đói lớn xảy ra ở xứ ấy. Thức ăn rất khan hiếm, và anh không có những thứ mình cần.

decisions.choice: a severe famine: a great shortage of food across the land
alternatives: a time of high prices only
decisions.reason: Famines came when the rains failed or crops were ruined (Genesis 41:54-57; Acts 11:28). The story makes his ruin complete: his money is gone just when food is scarce.

decisions.choice: to be in need: to lack what he needed to live
decisions.reason: The verb means to fall short or lack. It is the start of real hunger (15:17).

decisions.choice: There was very little food
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word "famine".

source.text: καὶ πορευθεὶς ἐκολλήθη ἑνὶ τῶν πολιτῶν τῆς χώρας ἐκείνης, καὶ ἔπεμψεν αὐτὸν εἰς τοὺς ἀγροὺς αὐτοῦ βόσκειν χοίρους·

records.literal_gloss: And having gone he joined himself to one of the citizens of the country that, and he sent him into the fields of him to feed pigs.

en.L: And going, he attached himself to one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him into his fields to feed pigs.
en.B: So he went and attached himself to one of the people of that country, and the man sent him out into his fields to look after pigs.
en.R: So he went to work for a man who lived in that country. The man sent him into his fields to feed his pigs.

es.L: Y yendo, se pegó a uno de los ciudadanos de aquel país, y lo envió a sus campos a alimentar cerdos.
es.B: Así que fue y se aferró a uno de los habitantes de aquel país, y el hombre lo mandó a sus campos a cuidar cerdos.
es.R: Entonces se fue a trabajar para un hombre que vivía en aquel país. El hombre lo mandó a sus campos a dar de comer a sus cerdos.

fr.L: Et, s’en étant allé, il s’est attaché à l’un des citoyens de ce pays-là, et celui-ci l’a envoyé dans ses champs faire paître des porcs.
fr.B: Il est donc allé se mettre au service d’un des habitants de ce pays, et l’homme l’a envoyé dans ses champs garder les porcs.
fr.R: Alors il est allé travailler pour un homme de ce pays. L’homme l’a envoyé dans ses champs pour nourrir ses cochons.

sw.L: Naye akienda, akajiambatanisha na mmoja wa wenyeji wa nchi ile, naye akamtuma mashambani mwake kuchunga nguruwe.
sw.B: Basi alikwenda akajishikiza kwa mmoja wa wenyeji wa nchi ile, na mtu huyo akamtuma mashambani mwake akachunge nguruwe.
sw.R: Basi alikwenda kufanya kazi kwa mtu mmoja aliyeishi katika nchi ile. Mtu huyo alimtuma mashambani mwake kulisha nguruwe wake.

vi.L: Và anh đi đến bám lấy một người dân của xứ ấy, và người ấy sai anh ra đồng mình để chăn heo.
vi.B: Vậy anh đến nương nhờ một người dân trong xứ ấy, và người này sai anh ra đồng chăn heo.
vi.R: Vì vậy anh đến làm công cho một người ở xứ ấy. Người này sai anh ra đồng để cho heo của ông ăn.

decisions.choice: attached himself to: went to him and would not let go, as one who begs for work
decisions.reason: The verb means to be glued or joined to. He pressed himself on a stranger to get any work at all.

decisions.choice: to feed pigs: the lowest work a Jewish man could imagine
decisions.reason: The law of Moses called pigs unclean (Leviticus 11:7; Deuteronomy 14:8). A Jew who fed pigs for a Gentile had fallen as low as he could.

decisions.choice: the man
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear who sent whom.

decisions.choice: se pegó a (L); se aferró a (B)
decisions.reason: The verb is to stick or cling to someone, as one who begs for work and will not let go (meaning decision m1). "Se pegó" keeps the picture; Balanced "se aferró" says the same in a more careful register.

decisions.choice: "bám lấy" (L); "nương nhờ" (B); "làm công cho" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says he went to the man and would not let go, as one who begs for work; each level says that more plainly.

source.text: καὶ ἐπεθύμει γεμίσαι τὴν κοιλίαν αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῶν κερατίων ὧν ἤσθιον οἱ χοῖροι, καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐδίδου αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And he was longing to fill the belly of him from the pods that were eating the pigs, and no one was giving to him.

en.L: And he was longing to fill his belly from the pods that the pigs were eating, and no one was giving [anything] to him.
en.B: He wished he could fill himself up with the carob pods the pigs were eating, but no one gave him a thing.
en.R: He was so hungry that he wanted to eat the bean pods that the pigs were eating. But no one gave him any food.

es.L: Y ansiaba llenar su estómago con las vainas que comían los cerdos, y nadie le daba [nada].
es.B: Él habría querido saciarse con las algarrobas que comían los cerdos, pero nadie le daba nada.
es.R: Tenía tanta hambre que quería comerse las vainas que comían los cerdos. Pero nadie le daba comida.

fr.L: Et il désirait remplir son ventre des caroubes que mangeaient les porcs, et personne ne lui [en] donnait.
fr.B: Il aurait bien voulu se remplir le ventre des gousses de caroube que mangeaient les porcs, mais personne ne lui donnait rien.
fr.R: Il avait tellement faim qu’il aurait voulu manger les cosses que mangeaient les cochons. Mais personne ne lui donnait à manger.

sw.L: Naye alikuwa akitamani kujaza tumbo lake kwa maganda ambayo nguruwe walikuwa wakiyala, na hakuna aliyekuwa akimpa [chochote].
sw.B: Alitamani sana kushiba kwa yale maganda ya mkarobu ambayo nguruwe walikula, lakini hakuna mtu aliyempa chochote.
sw.R: Alikuwa na njaa sana hata akatamani kula maganda ambayo nguruwe walikuwa wakila. Lakini hakuna mtu aliyempa chakula.

vi.L: Và anh ao ước lấp đầy bụng mình bằng những vỏ đậu mà heo ăn, và không ai cho anh [gì].
vi.B: Anh thèm được ăn cho no những trái đậu heo ăn, nhưng chẳng ai cho anh gì cả.
vi.R: Anh đói đến nỗi muốn ăn những trái đậu mà heo đang ăn. Nhưng không ai cho anh thứ gì để ăn cả.

decisions.choice: pods: the pods of the carob tree, used to feed animals
decisions.reason: Carob pods are long, sweet and tough. They were fed to animals, and only the very poor ate them.

decisions.choice: to fill his belly (SBLGNT)
alternatives: to be fed, to be satisfied
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "to fill his belly". Some early ones, among them Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus, read "to be satisfied" from the pods. The meaning is much the same: he was starving. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: no one was giving to him: no one gave him food, not even the pods
decisions.reason: The verb has no object. Its point is that no one cared for him at all.

decisions.choice: [anything]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the object English needs.

decisions.choice: carob pods (B); bean pods (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced names the plant; Readable describes it.

decisions.choice: vainas (L, R); algarrobas (B)
decisions.reason: The pods of the carob tree, used to feed animals (meaning decision m1). Spanish "algarrobas" names them exactly, at Balanced as the English says "carob pods"; Literal and Readable say only "pods".

decisions.choice: maganda ya mkarobu
decisions.reason: The pods of the carob tree (meaning decision m1), named at Balanced as the English says "carob pods". The carob tree is not widely known in East Africa, and a reviewer should confirm whether "mkarobu" is understood or plain "maganda" is better.

decisions.choice: "vỏ đậu" (L); "trái đậu" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The pods of the carob tree (meaning decision); the Vietnamese name of the tree is not widely known, so the text says bean pods, as the English Readable does.

source.text: εἰς ἑαυτὸν δὲ ἐλθὼν ἔφη· Πόσοι μίσθιοι τοῦ πατρός μου περισσεύονται ἄρτων, ἐγὼ δὲ λιμῷ ὧδε ἀπόλλυμαι·

records.literal_gloss: To himself however having come he was saying, How many hired servants of the father of me have abundance of bread, I however with hunger here am perishing!

en.L: But coming to himself, he said, 'How many of my father's hired workers have more than enough bread, but I am perishing here with hunger!
en.B: At last he saw his situation clearly. 'So many of my father's hired workers have more bread than they can eat,' he said, 'while I am dying of hunger here!
en.R: Then he began to think clearly. He said to himself, 'My father has many hired workers, and they all have more food than they need. But here I am, about to die because I have nothing to eat!

es.L: Pero, viniendo en sí, dijo: “¡Cuántos jornaleros de mi padre tienen pan de sobra, mientras yo aquí estoy pereciendo de hambre!
es.B: Por fin vio con claridad su situación. “Tantos jornaleros de mi padre tienen más pan del que pueden comer —se dijo—, ¡y yo aquí me muero de hambre!
es.R: Entonces empezó a pensar con claridad. Se dijo a sí mismo: “Mi padre tiene muchos trabajadores a sueldo, y todos tienen más comida de la que necesitan. ¡Y aquí estoy yo, a punto de morir porque no tengo nada que comer!

fr.L: Mais, rentrant en lui-même, il a dit : “Combien d’ouvriers de mon père ont du pain en abondance, et moi, ici, je meurs de faim !
fr.B: Alors il a vu clairement où il en était. “Tant d’ouvriers de mon père ont plus de pain qu’il ne leur en faut, s’est-il dit, et moi, ici, je meurs de faim !
fr.R: Alors il a commencé à réfléchir. Il s’est dit : “Mon père a beaucoup d’ouvriers, et ils ont tous plus à manger qu’il ne leur en faut. Et moi, je suis ici, en train de mourir parce que je n’ai rien à manger !

sw.L: Lakini alipojirudia mwenyewe, akasema, 'Ni vibarua wangapi wa baba yangu walio na mikate tele, nami hapa ninaangamia kwa njaa!
sw.B: Hatimaye akili zake zilimrudia. Akasema, 'Vibarua wengi wa baba yangu wana mikate kuliko wanavyoweza kula, na mimi hapa ninakufa kwa njaa!
sw.R: Kisha alianza kufikiri vizuri. Alijiambia, 'Baba yangu ana vibarua wengi, na wote wana chakula kuliko wanavyohitaji. Lakini mimi niko hapa, karibu kufa kwa sababu sina chochote cha kula!

vi.L: Nhưng khi tỉnh ngộ, anh nói: 'Biết bao người làm thuê của cha tôi có bánh ăn dư dật, còn tôi thì ở đây chết đói!
vi.B: Cuối cùng anh tỉnh ngộ và nói: 'Biết bao người làm thuê của cha tôi có bánh ăn dư thừa, còn tôi thì ở đây sắp chết đói!
vi.R: Rồi anh bắt đầu suy nghĩ cho sáng suốt. Anh tự nhủ: 'Cha tôi có nhiều người làm thuê, và họ đều có thức ăn dư thừa. Còn tôi ở đây sắp chết vì không có gì ăn!

decisions.choice: coming to himself: coming to his senses, seeing clearly
decisions.reason: The phrase was used of someone who returns to a right mind. It is the turning point of his story; what follows shows what it led to.

decisions.choice: hired workers: day laborers paid wages, not slaves of the household
decisions.reason: The word is different from the word for slaves in 15:22. Hired workers were paid by the day and had no place in the family (Matthew 20:1-2). Even they ate well at his father's house.

decisions.choice: perishing: dying
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for the lost sheep and coin (15:4, 9). Here it has its plain meaning: he is starving.

decisions.choice: how many: an exclamation, not a question
alternatives: a question asking for a number
decisions.reason: He is not counting; he is amazed at the plenty in his father's house.

decisions.choice: he saw his situation clearly (B); he began to think clearly (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the idiom, which Literal keeps.

decisions.choice: his words open here and run on to 15:19
decisions.reason: The Greek goes straight on from what he says to what he will do and say.

decisions.choice: jornaleros (L, B); trabajadores a sueldo (R)
decisions.reason: Day labourers paid wages, not slaves of the household (meaning decision m2), so they are kept apart from the "siervos" of 15:22 and the "criados" of 15:26.

decisions.choice: rentrant en lui-même (L)
decisions.reason: French has the idiom "rentrer en soi-même", to turn one's thoughts inward and see clearly, so Literal can keep the Greek image (m1). "Revenir à soi" would mean waking from a faint.

decisions.choice: vibarua
decisions.reason: Day labourers paid wages, not slaves of the household (meaning decision m2). "Kibarua" is exactly a casual worker paid by the day, and keeps them apart from the "watumwa" / "watumishi" of 15:22.

decisions.choice: "tỉnh ngộ" (L, B) for "coming to himself"; "người làm thuê" for the hired workers
decisions.reason: "tỉnh ngộ" is the Vietnamese for coming to one's senses and seeing clearly (meaning decision). "người làm thuê" are day laborers paid wages, kept apart from the household servants of 15:22.

decisions.choice: the son says "tôi" when he speaks to himself
decisions.reason: The plain first person; "ta" is kept for Jesus and for masters in the parables.

source.text: ἀναστὰς πορεύσομαι πρὸς τὸν πατέρα μου καὶ ἐρῶ αὐτῷ· Πάτερ, ἥμαρτον εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ ἐνώπιόν σου, οὐκέτι εἰμὶ ἄξιος κληθῆναι υἱός σου· ποίησόν με ὡς ἕνα τῶν μισθίων σου.

records.literal_gloss: Having risen up I will go to the father of me and I will say to him, Father, I have sinned against the heaven and before you; \v 19 no longer am I worthy to be called son of you; make me like one of the hired servants of you.

en.L: Getting up, I will go to my father and will say to him, "Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you; \v 19 I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired workers."'
en.B: I will get up and go back to my father, and I will tell him, "Father, I have sinned against heaven and in your sight. \v 19 I do not deserve to be called your son any longer. Take me on as one of your hired workers."'
en.R: I will leave this place and go back to my father. I will say to him, "Father, I have sinned against God and against you. \v 19 I am not good enough to be called your son anymore. Please let me be one of the workers you pay."'

es.L: Levantándome, iré a mi padre y le diré: ‘Padre, pequé contra el cielo y delante de ti; \v 19 ya no soy digno de ser llamado hijo tuyo; hazme igual que uno de tus jornaleros’”.
es.B: Me pondré en camino, volveré a mi padre y le diré: ‘Padre, he pecado contra el cielo y ante tus ojos. \v 19 Ya no merezco que se me llame hijo tuyo. Recíbeme como uno de tus jornaleros’”.
es.R: Me iré de este lugar y volveré a mi padre. Le diré: ‘Padre, he pecado contra Dios y contra ti. \v 19 No soy lo bastante bueno para que me llamen tu hijo. Por favor, déjame ser uno de los trabajadores a los que les pagas’”.

fr.L: M’étant levé, j’irai vers mon père et je lui dirai : ‘Père, j’ai péché contre le ciel et devant toi ; \v 19 je ne suis plus digne d’être appelé ton fils ; traite-moi comme l’un de tes ouvriers.’”
fr.B: Je vais me lever et retourner chez mon père, et je lui dirai : ‘Père, j’ai péché contre le ciel et envers toi. \v 19 Je ne mérite plus d’être appelé ton fils. Prends-moi comme l’un de tes ouvriers.’”
fr.R: Je vais quitter cet endroit et retourner chez mon père. Je lui dirai : ‘Père, j’ai péché contre Dieu et contre toi. \v 19 Je ne mérite plus que tu m’appelles ton fils. Je t’en prie, prends-moi comme un des ouvriers que tu paies.’”

sw.L: Nikiinuka, nitakwenda kwa baba yangu na kumwambia, "Baba, nimetenda dhambi dhidi ya mbingu na mbele yako; \v 19 sistahili tena kuitwa mwanao; unifanye kama mmoja wa vibarua wako."'
sw.B: Nitainuka nirudi kwa baba yangu, nimwambie, "Baba, nimetenda dhambi dhidi ya mbingu na machoni pako. \v 19 Sistahili tena kuitwa mwanao. Nipokee niwe mmoja wa vibarua wako."'
sw.R: Nitaondoka mahali hapa, nirudi kwa baba yangu. Nitamwambia, "Baba, nimetenda dhambi dhidi ya Mungu na dhidi yako. \v 19 Sifai tena kuitwa mwanao. Tafadhali, niruhusu niwe mmoja wa wafanyakazi unaowalipa."'

vi.L: Tôi sẽ đứng dậy, đi về với cha tôi và thưa với cha: "Thưa cha, con đã phạm tội với trời và trước mặt cha; \v 19 con không còn đáng được gọi là con của cha nữa; xin cha coi con như một người làm thuê của cha."'
vi.B: Tôi sẽ đứng dậy trở về với cha tôi và thưa: "Thưa cha, con đã phạm tội với trời và trước mặt cha. \v 19 Con không còn đáng được gọi là con của cha nữa. Xin cha nhận con làm một người làm thuê của cha."'
vi.R: Tôi sẽ rời khỏi chỗ này và trở về với cha tôi. Tôi sẽ thưa với cha: "Thưa cha, con đã phạm tội với Đức Chúa Trời và với cha. \v 19 Con không còn xứng đáng được gọi là con của cha nữa. Xin cha cho con làm một người làm công được cha trả lương."'

decisions.choice: against heaven: against God
decisions.reason: Out of reverence, Jewish speech often said "heaven" in place of God's name (15:7; Daniel 4:26). He has wronged God and his father both.

decisions.choice: I have sinned against ... and before you: the language of confession in Scripture
decisions.reason: Pharaoh used similar words to Moses (Exodus 10:16), and David confessed his sin against the Lord (2 Samuel 12:13; Psalm 51:6).

decisions.choice: worthy to be called your son: fit to be treated as a son
decisions.reason: He knows he has thrown away the place of a son. He hopes only for the place of a hired worker.

decisions.choice: hired workers: day laborers paid wages
decisions.reason: As in 15:17.

decisions.choice: against God
decisions.reason: Readable names God, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: his words close here; the words he plans to say are in double quotation marks
decisions.reason: The words he will say to his father are a quotation inside his own words.

decisions.choice: "trời" (L, B); "Đức Chúa Trời" (R)
decisions.reason: "Heaven" stands for God (meaning decision); Vietnamese "trời" carries the same reverent way of speaking of God, and Readable names him, as the English Readable does. Kept in 15:21.

source.text: καὶ ἀναστὰς ἦλθεν πρὸς τὸν πατέρα ἑαυτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And having risen up he went to the father of himself.

en.L: And getting up, he went to his own father.
en.B: So he set off and went back to his father.
en.R: So he got up and started back home to his father.

es.L: Y levantándose, se fue hacia su propio padre.
es.B: Así que se puso en camino y volvió a su padre.
es.R: Entonces se levantó y emprendió el regreso a casa, donde estaba su padre.

fr.L: Et, s’étant levé, il est allé vers son père.
fr.B: Il s’est donc mis en route et il est retourné chez son père.
fr.R: Alors il s’est levé et il a repris la route de la maison, pour retourner chez son père.

sw.L: Naye akainuka, akaenda kwa baba yake mwenyewe.
sw.B: Basi alianza safari, akarudi kwa baba yake.
sw.R: Basi aliondoka, akaanza kurudi nyumbani kwa baba yake.

vi.L: Và đứng dậy, anh đi về với cha mình.
vi.B: Vậy anh lên đường trở về với cha.
vi.R: Vậy anh đứng dậy và lên đường trở về nhà với cha.

decisions.choice: having risen up, he went: he did what he had said he would do (15:18)
alternatives: he stood up from where he sat
decisions.reason: The same words as his plan in 15:18. "Rising up" here means setting out.

decisions.choice: set off (B); got up and started back home (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of starting out.

source.text: ἔτι δὲ αὐτοῦ μακρὰν ἀπέχοντος εἶδεν αὐτὸν ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐσπλαγχνίσθη καὶ δραμὼν ἐπέπεσεν ἐπὶ τὸν τράχηλον αὐτοῦ καὶ κατεφίλησεν αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: Still now he far being distant saw him the father of him and was moved with compassion, and having run he fell upon the neck of him and kissed him.

en.L: But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was moved with compassion, and running, he fell upon his neck and kissed him.
en.B: His father caught sight of him while he was still far away, and his heart went out to him. He ran to meet him, embraced him and kissed him warmly.
en.R: While the son was still far down the road, his father saw him coming. He felt great love and pity for his son. He ran to him, hugged him, and kissed him again and again.

es.L: Pero estando él todavía lejos, su padre lo vio y se le conmovieron las entrañas, y corriendo, cayó sobre su cuello y lo besó efusivamente.
es.B: Su padre lo vio cuando todavía estaba lejos, y se le enterneció el corazón. Corrió a su encuentro, lo abrazó y lo besó con cariño.
es.R: El hijo todavía estaba lejos en el camino cuando su padre lo vio venir. Sintió un gran amor y una gran compasión por su hijo. Corrió hacia él, lo abrazó y lo besó una y otra vez.

fr.L: Mais alors qu’il était encore loin, son père l’a vu et a été ému de compassion ; et, courant, il s’est jeté à son cou et l’a couvert de baisers.
fr.B: Il était encore loin quand son père l’a aperçu, le cœur rempli de pitié. Il a couru à sa rencontre, l’a serré dans ses bras et l’a embrassé avec tendresse.
fr.R: Le fils était encore loin sur la route quand son père l’a vu arriver. Il a ressenti un grand amour et une grande pitié pour son fils. Il a couru vers lui, l’a pris dans ses bras et l’a embrassé encore et encore.

sw.L: Lakini yeye akiwa bado yuko mbali, baba yake alimwona na kuguswa moyoni kwa huruma; akakimbia, akajitupa shingoni pake na kumbusu.
sw.B: Baba yake alimwona akiwa bado mbali, na moyo wake ukajaa huruma. Akakimbia kumlaki, akamkumbatia na kumbusu kwa upendo.
sw.R: Mwana alipokuwa bado yuko mbali barabarani, baba yake alimwona akija. Alimpenda sana na kumhurumia mwanawe. Alikimbia kwake, akamkumbatia, akambusu tena na tena.

vi.L: Nhưng khi anh còn ở đằng xa, cha anh đã thấy anh và động lòng thương xót, chạy đến ôm choàng lấy cổ anh mà hôn.
vi.B: Anh còn ở đằng xa thì cha anh đã trông thấy, và ông động lòng thương xót. Ông chạy đến ôm chầm lấy anh và hôn anh thắm thiết.
vi.R: Khi người con còn ở đằng xa trên đường, cha anh đã thấy anh đang về. Ông rất thương xót con. Ông chạy đến ôm chầm lấy con, và hôn con mãi.

decisions.choice: was moved with compassion: was stirred to the depths by love and pity
alternatives: felt sorry in a distant way
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for a person's inward parts, where deep feelings were felt. Luke uses it of Jesus at Nain (7:13) and of the Samaritan (10:33).

decisions.choice: while he was still far off, his father saw him: the father was watching for him
decisions.reason: The father sees him first and runs to him before the son can say a word. The text does not say he had been watching, but the story suggests it.

decisions.choice: fell upon his neck: threw his arms around him
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of a warm embrace, as when Esau met Jacob (Genesis 33:4) and Joseph met his father (Genesis 46:29).

decisions.choice: kissed: kissed warmly, again and again
decisions.reason: The verb is a stronger form of the usual word for a kiss (7:38, 45).

decisions.choice: having run: an older man running to meet his son
decisions.reason: A head of a household did not usually run. The father puts dignity aside to reach his son.

decisions.choice: his heart went out to him
decisions.reason: Balanced uses an everyday phrase for the deep feeling, as in 10:33.

decisions.choice: se le conmovieron las entrañas (L); se le enterneció el corazón (B)
decisions.reason: The verb is formed from the word for the inner parts, the seat of deep feeling (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps "entrañas", as for that noun elsewhere; Balanced says "corazón", the Spanish seat of the same feeling.

decisions.choice: il s’est jeté à son cou (L)
alternatives: il est tombé sur son cou
decisions.reason: French "se jeter au cou de quelqu’un" is the same image as the Greek and means to throw one's arms around him (m3); "tomber sur son cou" is not French.

decisions.choice: "động lòng thương xót" (L, B); "rất thương xót" (R)
decisions.reason: The same words as for the Samaritan in 10:33, for the same Greek verb.

decisions.choice: "ôm choàng lấy cổ" (L) for "fell upon his neck"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the neck; a word-for-word "fell" would not be understood in Vietnamese as an embrace, which is what the meaning decision says it is.

source.text: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ υἱὸς αὐτῷ· Πάτερ, ἥμαρτον εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ ἐνώπιόν σου, οὐκέτι εἰμὶ ἄξιος κληθῆναι υἱός σου.

records.literal_gloss: Said then the son to him, Father, I have sinned against the heaven and before you, no longer am I worthy to be called son of you.

en.L: And the son said to him, 'Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you; I am no longer worthy to be called your son.'
en.B: His son said to him, 'Father, I have sinned against heaven and in your sight. I do not deserve to be called your son any longer.'
en.R: The son said, 'Father, I have sinned against God and against you. I am not good enough to be called your son anymore.'

es.L: Y el hijo le dijo: “Padre, pequé contra el cielo y delante de ti; ya no soy digno de ser llamado hijo tuyo”.
es.B: Su hijo le dijo: “Padre, he pecado contra el cielo y ante tus ojos. Ya no merezco que se me llame hijo tuyo”.
es.R: El hijo le dijo: “Padre, he pecado contra Dios y contra ti. No soy lo bastante bueno para que me llamen tu hijo”.

fr.L: Et le fils lui a dit : “Père, j’ai péché contre le ciel et devant toi ; je ne suis plus digne d’être appelé ton fils.”
fr.B: Son fils lui a dit : “Père, j’ai péché contre le ciel et envers toi. Je ne mérite plus d’être appelé ton fils.”
fr.R: Le fils a dit : “Père, j’ai péché contre Dieu et contre toi. Je ne mérite plus que tu m’appelles ton fils.”

sw.L: Na mwana akamwambia, 'Baba, nimetenda dhambi dhidi ya mbingu na mbele yako; sistahili tena kuitwa mwanao.'
sw.B: Mwanawe alimwambia, 'Baba, nimetenda dhambi dhidi ya mbingu na machoni pako. Sistahili tena kuitwa mwanao.'
sw.R: Mwana alisema, 'Baba, nimetenda dhambi dhidi ya Mungu na dhidi yako. Sifai tena kuitwa mwanao.'

vi.L: Và người con nói với cha: 'Thưa cha, con đã phạm tội với trời và trước mặt cha; con không còn đáng được gọi là con của cha nữa.'
