vi.B: Người con thưa: 'Thưa cha, con đã phạm tội với trời và trước mặt cha. Con không còn đáng được gọi là con của cha nữa.'
vi.R: Người con nói: 'Thưa cha, con đã phạm tội với Đức Chúa Trời và với cha. Con không còn xứng đáng được gọi là con của cha nữa.'

decisions.choice: the son's words end with "your son" (SBLGNT)
alternatives: the son's words go on: "make me like one of your hired workers"
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts, among them Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus, add the last line of the speech he planned (15:19). Most manuscripts do not have it, and it may have been added to match 15:19. Without it, the father breaks in before the son can ask to be a hired worker. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: against heaven: against God
decisions.reason: As in 15:18.

decisions.choice: against God
decisions.reason: As in 15:18.

source.text: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ πατὴρ πρὸς τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ· Ταχὺ ἐξενέγκατε στολὴν τὴν πρώτην καὶ ἐνδύσατε αὐτόν, καὶ δότε δακτύλιον εἰς τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ καὶ ὑποδήματα εἰς τοὺς πόδας, καὶ φέρετε τὸν μόσχον τὸν σιτευτόν, θύσατε, καὶ φαγόντες εὐφρανθῶμεν, ὅτι οὗτος ὁ υἱός μου νεκρὸς ἦν καὶ ἀνέζησεν, ἦν ἀπολωλὼς καὶ εὑρέθη.

records.literal_gloss: Said then the father to the slaves of him, Quickly bring out a robe the best and clothe him, and give a ring for the hand of him and sandals for the feet, \v 23 and bring the calf the fattened, kill [it], and having eaten let us be merry, \v 24 for this the son of me dead was and is alive again, he was lost and is found.

en.L: But the father said to his slaves, 'Quickly, bring out a robe, the best [one], and clothe him, and give [him] a ring for his hand and sandals for [his] feet, \v 23 and bring the fattened calf, kill [it], and let us eat and celebrate, \v 24 because this son of mine was dead and has come to life again; he was lost and has been found.'
en.B: But the father said to his servants, 'Hurry! Bring out the finest robe and dress him in it. Give him a ring for his hand and sandals for his feet. \v 23 Fetch the calf we have been fattening and slaughter it. Let us eat and celebrate, \v 24 for my son here was dead, and now he lives again. He was lost, and now he has been found.'
en.R: But the father called to his servants, 'Be quick! Go and get the best robe we have and put it on my son. Give him a ring to wear on his hand, and sandals for his feet. \v 23 Bring the calf that we have been feeding to make it fat, and kill it. We will have a big meal and a party! \v 24 My son here was dead, but he is alive again. He was lost, but now he is found.'

es.L: Pero el padre dijo a sus esclavos: “Pronto, {{plural_you:saquen|sacad}} un manto, el mejor, y {{plural_you:vístanlo|vestidlo}}, y {{plural_you:denle|dadle}} un anillo para su mano y sandalias para [sus] pies, \v 23 y {{plural_you:traigan|traed}} el ternero cebado, {{plural_you:mátenlo|matadlo}}, y comiendo, hagamos fiesta, \v 24 porque este hijo mío muerto estaba y revivió, estaba perdido y fue hallado”.
es.B: Pero el padre dijo a sus siervos: “¡Rápido! {{plural_you:Traigan|Traed}} el mejor manto y {{plural_you:vístanlo|vestidlo}} con él. {{plural_you:Pónganle|Ponedle}} un anillo en la mano y {{plural_you:denle|dadle}} sandalias para los pies. \v 23 {{plural_you:Busquen|Buscad}} el ternero que hemos estado engordando y {{plural_you:mátenlo|matadlo}}. Comamos y hagamos fiesta, \v 24 porque mi hijo, aquí presente, estaba muerto y vive otra vez; se había perdido y ha sido encontrado”.
es.R: Pero el padre llamó a sus siervos: “¡{{plural_you:Dense prisa|Daos prisa}}! {{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} a buscar el mejor manto que tengamos y {{plural_you:pónganselo|ponédselo}} a mi hijo. {{plural_you:Pónganle|Ponedle}} un anillo en la mano y {{plural_you:denle|dadle}} sandalias para los pies. \v 23 {{plural_you:Traigan|Traed}} el ternero que hemos estado alimentando para engordarlo, y {{plural_you:mátenlo|matadlo}}. ¡Vamos a hacer un gran banquete y una fiesta! \v 24 Mi hijo estaba muerto, pero ha vuelto a vivir. Estaba perdido, y ahora ha aparecido”.

fr.L: Mais le père a dit à ses esclaves : “Vite, apportez une robe, la plus belle, et habillez-le ; et donnez[-lui] un anneau pour sa main et des sandales pour [ses] pieds ; \v 23 et amenez le veau gras, tuez[-le], et mangeons et réjouissons-nous, \v 24 car mon fils que voici était mort et il est revenu à la vie ; il était perdu et il a été retrouvé.”
fr.B: Mais le père a dit à ses serviteurs : “Vite ! Apportez la plus belle robe et mettez-la-lui. Donnez-lui une bague pour son doigt et des sandales pour ses pieds. \v 23 Allez chercher le veau que nous avons engraissé et tuez-le. Mangeons et faisons la fête, \v 24 car mon fils que voilà était mort, et maintenant il revit. Il était perdu, et maintenant il est retrouvé.”
fr.R: Mais le père a appelé ses serviteurs : “Vite ! Allez chercher la plus belle robe que nous avons et mettez-la à mon fils. Donnez-lui une bague à porter au doigt et des sandales pour ses pieds. \v 23 Amenez le veau que nous avons nourri pour le rendre bien gras, et tuez-le. Nous allons faire un grand repas et une grande fête ! \v 24 Mon fils que voici était mort, mais il est de nouveau vivant. Il était perdu, mais maintenant on l’a retrouvé.”

sw.L: Baba naye akawaambia watumwa wake, 'Haraka, toeni joho, lile lililo bora, mkamvike, na mpeni pete kwa ajili ya mkono wake na viatu kwa ajili ya miguu [yake], \v 23 na mleteni ndama aliyenenepeshwa, mchinjeni, nasi tule na tusherehekee, \v 24 kwa sababu huyu mwanangu alikuwa mfu, naye amerudi uzimani; alikuwa amepotea, naye amepatikana.'
sw.B: Lakini baba aliwaambia watumishi wake, 'Harakisheni! Leteni joho lililo bora kuliko yote, mkamvike. Mvalisheni pete mkononi na viatu miguuni. \v 23 Mleteni ndama tuliyekuwa tukimnenepesha, mchinjeni. Tule na kusherehekea, \v 24 kwa maana mwanangu huyu alikuwa amekufa, na sasa yu hai tena. Alikuwa amepotea, na sasa amepatikana.'
sw.R: Lakini baba aliwaita watumishi wake, 'Fanyeni haraka! Nendeni mkalete joho lililo bora kuliko yote tulilo nalo, mkamvike mwanangu. Mpeni pete avae mkononi, na viatu vya kuvaa miguuni. \v 23 Mleteni ndama tuliyekuwa tukimlisha ili anenepe, mkamchinje. Tutakuwa na karamu kubwa na sherehe! \v 24 Mwanangu huyu alikuwa amekufa, lakini yu hai tena. Alikuwa amepotea, lakini sasa amepatikana.'

vi.L: Nhưng người cha bảo các nô lệ mình: 'Hãy mau đem áo choàng, cái tốt nhất, ra mặc cho nó, đeo nhẫn vào tay nó và mang dép vào chân [nó], \v 23 rồi đem con bê béo ra, làm thịt đi, và chúng ta hãy ăn mừng, \v 24 vì đứa con trai này của ta đã chết mà nay sống lại, đã mất mà nay đã tìm thấy.'
vi.B: Nhưng người cha bảo các đầy tớ: 'Mau lên! Hãy đem chiếc áo choàng đẹp nhất ra mặc cho nó. Đeo nhẫn vào tay nó và mang dép vào chân nó. \v 23 Hãy dắt con bê đã vỗ béo ra làm thịt. Chúng ta hãy ăn mừng, \v 24 vì con trai ta đây đã chết mà nay sống lại, đã mất mà nay lại tìm được.'
vi.R: Nhưng người cha gọi các đầy tớ: 'Nhanh lên! Hãy đi lấy chiếc áo đẹp nhất nhà ta mà mặc cho con ta. Hãy đeo nhẫn vào tay nó, và mang dép vào chân nó. \v 23 Hãy dắt con bê đã được nuôi cho béo ra mà làm thịt. Chúng ta sẽ ăn tiệc và vui mừng! \v 24 Con ta đây đã chết, nhưng nay sống lại. Nó đã bị mất, nhưng nay đã được tìm thấy.'

decisions.choice: slaves: members of the household who belonged to the father
decisions.reason: The word is the usual word for a slave, different from the hired workers of 15:17 and 19. The father has slaves at his command; the son had hoped only to be a hired worker.

decisions.choice: the best robe, a ring, sandals: signs that he is welcomed as a son with honor
alternatives: simple clothing for a poor man
decisions.reason: A fine robe was given to honor a person (Genesis 41:42; Esther 6:7-11). A ring could carry a family seal and showed standing in the household (Genesis 41:42). Slaves and hired workers often went barefoot; sandals marked a free son.

decisions.choice: the fattened calf: a calf kept and fed for a special feast
decisions.reason: Meat was rarely eaten in ordinary homes. A calf fattened on grain was kept for a great occasion and would feed a whole village (Genesis 18:7; 1 Samuel 28:24).

decisions.choice: was dead and has come to life; was lost and has been found: he was cut off from his father, and now he is restored
decisions.reason: The son had not died, but he was as good as dead to his family. The pairs pick up the lost sheep and coin (15:6, 9) and speak of the new life that comes when a sinner returns (15:7, 10).

decisions.choice: let us celebrate: let us feast and be glad together
decisions.reason: The verb means to be glad and merry, and is used of feasting (12:19; 16:19). The same verb is used in 15:24, 29 and 32.

decisions.choice: dress him in it (B); put it on my son (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use everyday wording for putting on the robe. The father tells the servants to "give" the ring and sandals, and all three levels keep that verb.

decisions.choice: We will have a big meal and a party!
alternatives: having eaten, let us be merry
decisions.reason: Readable uses everyday words for a feast and a celebration.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: esclavos (L); siervos (B, R)
decisions.reason: Members of the household who belonged to the father (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps "esclavos"; Balanced and Readable say "siervos", as the English says "servants", as through Luke.

decisions.choice: manto
decisions.reason: The long outer robe of honour (meaning decision m2). "Túnica" is kept for the garment worn next to the skin, as through Luke.

decisions.choice: esclaves (L); serviteurs (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English and the style guide: Literal keeps that these people belonged to the father (m1); Balanced and Readable say "serviteurs".

decisions.choice: watumwa (L); watumishi (B, R)
decisions.reason: Members of the household who belonged to the father (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps "watumwa"; Balanced and Readable say "watumishi", as the English says "servants", as through Luke.

decisions.choice: joho
decisions.reason: The long outer robe of honour (meaning decision m2). "Kanzu" is kept for the garment worn next to the skin, as through Luke.

decisions.choice: "nô lệ" (L); "đầy tớ" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The style guide's rule for doulos, as in 14:17.

decisions.choice: the father says "ta" to his servants and calls his son "nó"
decisions.reason: A householder speaking to his servants; "nó" is how a Vietnamese father speaks of his own child, with warmth, not scorn.

source.text: καὶ ἤρξαντο εὐφραίνεσθαι.

records.literal_gloss: And they began to be merry.

en.L: And they began to celebrate.
en.B: And the celebration began.
en.R: Then the party started.

es.L: Y comenzaron a celebrar.
es.B: Y dio comienzo la celebración.
es.R: Entonces empezó la fiesta.

fr.L: Et ils ont commencé à se réjouir.
fr.B: Et la fête a commencé.
fr.R: Alors la fête a démarré.

sw.L: Nao wakaanza kusherehekea.
sw.B: Basi sherehe ikaanza.
sw.R: Kisha karamu ikaanza.

vi.L: Và họ bắt đầu ăn mừng.
vi.B: Và cuộc vui bắt đầu.
vi.R: Rồi bữa tiệc bắt đầu.

decisions.choice: they began to be merry: the feast is under way when the elder son comes home
decisions.reason: "Began" leads into the next scene: the music and dancing are still going on in 15:25.

decisions.choice: the celebration began
decisions.reason: Balanced makes the celebration the subject; the meaning is the same.

source.text: Ἦν δὲ ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ ὁ πρεσβύτερος ἐν ἀγρῷ· καὶ ὡς ἐρχόμενος ἤγγισεν τῇ οἰκίᾳ, ἤκουσεν συμφωνίας καὶ χορῶν, καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος ἕνα τῶν παίδων ἐπυνθάνετο τί ἂν εἴη ταῦτα·

records.literal_gloss: Was now the son of him the elder in [the] field, and while coming he drew near to the house, he heard music and dancing, \v 26 and having called near one of the servants he was asking what might be these things.

en.L: Now his elder son was in the field, and as he came and drew near to the house, he heard music and dancing, \v 26 and calling one of the servants to [him], he asked what these things might be.
en.B: All this time the older son had been out in the field. On his way back, as he came close to the house, the sound of music and dancing reached him. \v 26 He called over one of the servants and asked him what this could mean.
en.R: The older son had been working out in the field. As he walked back toward the house, he could hear music and people dancing. \v 26 He called to one of the servants and asked what was happening.

es.L: Ahora bien, su hijo, el mayor, estaba en [el] campo; y cuando, viniendo, se acercó a la casa, oyó música y danzas, \v 26 y llamando junto a [sí] a uno de los muchachos, preguntaba qué sería aquello.
es.B: Mientras tanto, el hijo mayor había estado en el campo. Al volver, cuando ya estaba cerca de la casa, le llegó el sonido de la música y del baile. \v 26 Llamó a uno de los criados y le preguntó qué significaba todo aquello.
es.R: El hijo mayor había estado trabajando en el campo. Mientras volvía hacia la casa, oyó música y gente bailando. \v 26 Llamó a uno de los criados y le preguntó qué pasaba.

fr.L: Or son fils aîné était dans le champ ; et comme, en revenant, il approchait de la maison, il a entendu de la musique et des danses, \v 26 et, ayant appelé un des serviteurs, il s’informait de ce que cela pouvait être.
fr.B: Pendant ce temps, le fils aîné était aux champs. Sur le chemin du retour, comme il approchait de la maison, le bruit de la musique et des danses est parvenu jusqu’à lui. \v 26 Il a appelé un des serviteurs et lui a demandé ce que cela voulait dire.
fr.R: Le fils aîné était en train de travailler dans les champs. Il revenait vers la maison quand il a entendu de la musique et des gens qui dansaient. \v 26 Il a appelé un des serviteurs et lui a demandé ce qui se passait.

sw.L: Na mwanawe yule mkubwa alikuwa shambani; na alipokaribia nyumba akiwa njiani kuja, alisikia muziki na ngoma, \v 26 naye, akimwita mmoja wa vijana, akauliza ni mambo gani hayo.
sw.B: Wakati huo wote mwana mkubwa alikuwa shambani. Alipokuwa akirudi na kukaribia nyumba, sauti ya muziki na ngoma ikamfikia. \v 26 Akamwita mmoja wa watumishi, akamwuliza maana ya mambo hayo.
sw.R: Mwana mkubwa alikuwa akifanya kazi shambani. Alipokuwa akirudi nyumbani, alisikia muziki na watu wakicheza ngoma. \v 26 Alimwita mmoja wa watumishi na kumwuliza kilichokuwa kikitokea.

vi.L: Bấy giờ người con cả của ông đang ở ngoài đồng; và khi về gần đến nhà, anh nghe tiếng nhạc và tiếng nhảy múa, \v 26 và gọi một người giúp việc đến, anh hỏi những việc ấy là gì.
vi.B: Lúc ấy người con cả đang ở ngoài đồng. Trên đường về, khi đến gần nhà, anh nghe có tiếng nhạc và tiếng nhảy múa. \v 26 Anh gọi một người giúp việc lại và hỏi có chuyện gì vậy.
vi.R: Người con cả đang làm việc ngoài đồng. Khi đi về gần đến nhà, anh nghe tiếng nhạc và tiếng người ta nhảy múa. \v 26 Anh gọi một người giúp việc lại và hỏi chuyện gì đang xảy ra.

decisions.choice: his elder son was in the field: at work while the feast began
decisions.reason: The elder son is doing his daily work on the farm. He has stayed with his father the whole time (15:29, 31).

decisions.choice: music and dancing: the sounds of a feast
decisions.reason: The first word means music played or sung together; the second, dancing in a group, as at weddings and festivals.

decisions.choice: servants: young household servants or helpers
decisions.reason: The word can mean a child or a servant. Here it is one of the household staff. It is a different word from the slaves of 15:22 and the hired workers of 15:17.

decisions.choice: had been working out in the field
decisions.reason: Readable says why he was in the field, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: muchachos (L); criados (B, R)
decisions.reason: Young household servants or helpers (meaning decision m3), a different word from the "siervos" of 15:22. Literal keeps the sense of youth; Balanced and Readable say "criados".

decisions.choice: "người giúp việc" for Luke's word here
decisions.reason: Luke uses a different word from the "slaves" of 15:22, for young household servants or helpers (meaning decision); a different Vietnamese word keeps them apart.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὅτι Ὁ ἀδελφός σου ἥκει, καὶ ἔθυσεν ὁ πατήρ σου τὸν μόσχον τὸν σιτευτόν, ὅτι ὑγιαίνοντα αὐτὸν ἀπέλαβεν.

records.literal_gloss: He and said to him that, The brother of you is come, and has killed the father of you the calf the fattened, because in good health him he has received back.

en.L: And he said to him, 'Your brother has come, and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has received him back healthy.'
en.B: 'Your brother is home,' the servant told him, 'and your father has slaughtered the fattened calf, because his son has come back to him alive and well.'
en.R: The servant told him, 'Your brother has come home. Your father killed the calf that was being fattened for a feast, because your brother has come back to him safe and healthy.'

es.L: Y él le dijo: “Tu hermano ha venido, y tu padre ha matado el ternero cebado, porque lo ha recobrado sano”.
es.B: “Tu hermano está en casa —le dijo el criado—, y tu padre ha matado el ternero cebado, porque ha recuperado a su hijo con vida y con salud”.
es.R: El criado le dijo: “Tu hermano ha vuelto a casa. Tu padre mató el ternero que estaban engordando para una fiesta, porque tu hermano ha vuelto a él sano y salvo”.

fr.L: Et celui-ci lui a dit : “Ton frère est arrivé, et ton père a tué le veau gras, parce qu’il l’a recouvré en bonne santé.”
fr.B: “Ton frère est de retour, lui a dit le serviteur, et ton père a tué le veau gras, parce que son fils lui est revenu sain et sauf.”
fr.R: Le serviteur lui a répondu : “Ton frère est revenu à la maison. Ton père a tué le veau qu’on engraissait pour une fête, parce que ton frère lui est revenu en bonne santé.”

sw.L: Naye akamwambia, 'Ndugu yako amekuja, na baba yako amemchinja ndama aliyenenepeshwa, kwa sababu amemrudia akiwa mzima wa afya.'
sw.B: Mtumishi alimwambia, 'Ndugu yako amerudi nyumbani, na baba yako amemchinja yule ndama tuliyekuwa tukimnenepesha, kwa sababu mwanawe amemrudia salama salimini.'
sw.R: Mtumishi alimwambia, 'Ndugu yako amerudi nyumbani. Baba yako amemchinja ndama aliyekuwa akinenepeshwa kwa ajili ya karamu, kwa sababu ndugu yako amerudi kwake salama na mzima.'

vi.L: Người ấy nói với anh: 'Em cậu đã về, và cha cậu đã làm thịt con bê béo, vì ông đã nhận lại cậu ấy mạnh khỏe.'
vi.B: Người giúp việc thưa: 'Em cậu đã về, và cha cậu đã làm thịt con bê vỗ béo, vì ông đón được cậu ấy trở về bình an mạnh khỏe.'
vi.R: Người giúp việc thưa: 'Em cậu đã về nhà. Cha cậu đã làm thịt con bê được nuôi béo để ăn mừng, vì em cậu đã trở về với ông bình an và khỏe mạnh.'

decisions.choice: in good health: safe and well
decisions.reason: The servant reports only the outward facts: the son is alive and well. The father sees more: his son was dead and lives (15:24).

decisions.choice: has received him back: has him back again
alternatives: has taken him in as a guest
decisions.reason: The verb means to get back what was one's own.

decisions.choice: the servant (B, R); his son (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker, and Balanced names the one who came back, so that the pronouns stay clear.

decisions.choice: the servant says "tu" to the elder son
decisions.reason: French follows the Greek singular, as the style guide does for every address to one person; "vous" would add a social register the text does not mark.

decisions.choice: the servant calls the elder son "cậu" and the younger "cậu ấy"; "em cậu" for "your brother"
decisions.reason: "cậu" is how a household servant speaks to the master's grown son. Vietnamese must say whether a brother is older or younger; the younger son is meant, so "em".

source.text: ὠργίσθη δὲ καὶ οὐκ ἤθελεν εἰσελθεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: He was angry however and not was willing to go in.

en.L: But he became angry and was not willing to go in.
en.B: At this he grew angry and would not go inside.
en.R: The older son was angry. He would not go into the house.

es.L: Pero él se airó, y no quería entrar.
es.B: Ante esto se enojó y se negaba a entrar.
es.R: El hijo mayor se enojó mucho. No quería entrar en la casa.

fr.L: Mais il s’est mis en colère, et il ne voulait pas entrer.
fr.B: Alors il s’est fâché et il refusait d’entrer.
fr.R: Le fils aîné était en colère. Il ne voulait pas entrer dans la maison.

sw.L: Lakini alikasirika na hakuwa tayari kuingia.
sw.B: Hapo alikasirika, akakataa kabisa kuingia.
sw.R: Mwana mkubwa alikasirika. Hakutaka kuingia nyumbani.

vi.L: Nhưng anh nổi giận và không muốn vào.
vi.B: Anh nổi giận và nhất định không chịu vào nhà.
vi.R: Người con cả giận lắm. Anh không chịu vào nhà.

decisions.choice: was not willing to go in: he kept refusing
decisions.reason: The verb form shows a stubborn refusal. He shuts himself out of the feast, just as the grumblers of 15:2 will not share Jesus' table with sinners.

decisions.choice: The older son
decisions.reason: Readable names him.

source.text: ὁ δὲ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ ἐξελθὼν παρεκάλει αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: The and father of him having gone out was begging him.

en.L: And his father, coming out, was pleading with him.
en.B: His father came out and appealed to him.
en.R: So his father came out and begged him to come in.

es.L: Y su padre, saliendo, le suplicaba.
es.B: Su padre salió a rogarle.
es.R: Entonces su padre salió y le suplicó que entrara.

fr.L: Et son père, étant sorti, le suppliait.
fr.B: Son père est sorti et s’est mis à le supplier.
fr.R: Alors son père est sorti et l’a supplié d’entrer.

sw.L: Na baba yake, akitoka nje, alikuwa akimsihi.
sw.B: Baba yake alitoka nje akaja kumbembeleza.
sw.R: Basi baba yake alitoka nje, akamwomba sana aingie ndani.

vi.L: Và cha anh đi ra nài khuyên anh.
vi.B: Cha anh đi ra năn nỉ anh.
vi.R: Vì vậy cha anh đi ra năn nỉ anh vào.

decisions.choice: was pleading with: kept urging him, with warmth
decisions.reason: The verb can mean urge, appeal or comfort. Here the father goes out to his elder son, as he ran out to the younger, and appeals to him to come in.

decisions.choice: to come in
decisions.reason: Readable says what the father pleaded for.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν τῷ πατρὶ αὐτοῦ· Ἰδοὺ τοσαῦτα ἔτη δουλεύω σοι καὶ οὐδέποτε ἐντολήν σου παρῆλθον, καὶ ἐμοὶ οὐδέποτε ἔδωκας ἔριφον ἵνα μετὰ τῶν φίλων μου εὐφρανθῶ·

records.literal_gloss: He and answering said to the father of him, Behold, so many years I serve you and never a commandment of you I disobeyed, and to me never did you give a young goat that with the friends of me I might make merry.

en.L: But answering, he said to his father, 'Look, so many years I have been serving you as a slave, and I never disobeyed a command of yours, and you never gave me a young goat so that I might celebrate with my friends.
en.B: He replied to his father, 'Listen! For all these years I have worked like a slave for you. Not once have I gone against your orders. And not once have you given me a young goat for a feast with my friends.
en.R: But he said to his father, 'Look at all the years I have worked hard for you, like a slave! I have always done what you told me to do. But you never once gave me a young goat, so that I could have a party with my friends.

es.L: Pero él, respondiendo, dijo a su padre: “Mira, tantos años te sirvo como esclavo, y nunca transgredí un mandato tuyo, y a mí nunca me diste un cabrito para que celebrara con mis amigos.
es.B: Él le respondió a su padre: “¡Escucha! Todos estos años he trabajado como un esclavo para ti. Ni una sola vez he desobedecido tus órdenes. Y ni una sola vez me has dado un cabrito para hacer fiesta con mis amigos.
es.R: Pero él le dijo a su padre: “¡Mira todos los años que he trabajado duro para ti, como un esclavo! Siempre he hecho lo que me has mandado. Pero nunca me diste ni siquiera un cabrito para hacer una fiesta con mis amigos.

fr.L: Mais lui, répondant, a dit à son père : “Voici tant d’années que je te sers comme un esclave, et jamais je n’ai transgressé un de tes commandements ; et à moi, jamais tu n’as donné un chevreau pour que je fasse la fête avec mes amis.
fr.B: Il a répondu à son père : “Écoute ! Depuis tant d’années, je travaille pour toi comme un esclave. Pas une seule fois je n’ai désobéi à tes ordres. Et pas une seule fois tu ne m’as donné un chevreau pour faire la fête avec mes amis.
fr.R: Mais il a dit à son père : “Regarde toutes ces années où j’ai travaillé dur pour toi, comme un esclave ! J’ai toujours fait ce que tu m’as dit de faire. Mais tu ne m’as jamais donné, pas une seule fois, un petit chevreau pour que je fasse la fête avec mes amis.

sw.L: Lakini yeye akajibu, akamwambia baba yake, 'Tazama, miaka hii yote ninakutumikia kama mtumwa, na sijawahi kamwe kuiasi amri yako, nami hujawahi kunipa mwana-mbuzi ili nisherehekee pamoja na rafiki zangu.
sw.B: Alimjibu baba yake, 'Sikiliza! Miaka hii yote nimekufanyia kazi kama mtumwa. Sijawahi hata mara moja kukaidi maagizo yako. Nawe hujawahi hata mara moja kunipa mwana-mbuzi ili nifanye karamu na rafiki zangu.
sw.R: Lakini alimwambia baba yake, 'Angalia miaka yote niliyokufanyia kazi ngumu, kama mtumwa! Siku zote nimefanya ulichoniambia. Lakini hujawahi hata mara moja kunipa mwana-mbuzi ili nifanye sherehe na rafiki zangu.

vi.L: Nhưng anh đáp lời cha: 'Kìa, đã bao nhiêu năm nay con phục dịch cha như nô lệ, và chưa hề trái một mệnh lệnh nào của cha, vậy mà cha chưa hề cho con một con dê con để con vui chơi với bạn bè con.
vi.B: Anh trả lời cha: 'Cha xem đó! Bao nhiêu năm nay con làm lụng cho cha như một tên nô lệ. Chưa bao giờ con trái lệnh cha. Thế mà chưa bao giờ cha cho con một con dê con để ăn mừng với bạn bè con.
vi.R: Nhưng anh nói với cha: 'Cha xem, bao nhiêu năm nay con đã làm việc vất vả cho cha, chẳng khác gì một nô lệ! Con luôn làm theo mọi điều cha bảo. Vậy mà chưa một lần nào cha cho con một con dê con để con ăn tiệc với bạn bè.

decisions.choice: I have been serving you: working as a slave works
decisions.reason: The verb is formed from the word for a slave. He sees himself as a slave in his father's house, not as a son, though the father says all he has is his (15:31).

decisions.choice: a young goat: a small animal, worth much less than a fattened calf
decisions.reason: He compares the little he thinks he was given with the great feast for his brother.

decisions.choice: look: an outburst, calling attention to his complaint
alternatives: a word asking him to see something
decisions.reason: He does not greet his father with "Father", as the younger son did (15:21); he begins with a protest.

decisions.choice: Look (L); Listen! (B); Look at (R)
decisions.reason: "Behold" is old-fashioned. Here the word is an angry cry, so Balanced and Readable keep it as an outburst.

decisions.choice: serving you as a slave (L); worked like a slave (B, R)
decisions.reason: The words keep the link with the word for a slave, as the meaning decision explains. "Like a slave" stays at every level, as the style guide keeps "slave" where slavery itself is the point: the elder son sets himself as a slave against the son he is (15:31; meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: his words open here and run on to 15:30
decisions.reason: The elder son's complaint is one speech.

decisions.choice: Voici tant d’années que (L)
alternatives: Voici, tant d’années je te sers
decisions.reason: French "voici ... que" with the present says how long something has gone on, so Literal keeps the Greek particle and present tense in a natural sentence; Balanced and Readable make it the outburst the English has (m3).

decisions.choice: kama mtumwa
decisions.reason: The son says he has worked as a slave works (meaning decision m1); slavery itself is the comparison, so "mtumwa" stands at every level, as the English says "slave" at every level.

decisions.choice: "nô lệ" at every level
decisions.reason: The elder son's complaint is that he has been treated like a slave (meaning decision); the hard word is the point, as the English keeps "slave" at every level.

source.text: ὅτε δὲ ὁ υἱός σου οὗτος ὁ καταφαγών σου τὸν βίον μετὰ πορνῶν ἦλθεν, ἔθυσας αὐτῷ τὸν σιτευτὸν μόσχον.

records.literal_gloss: When however the son of you this, the [one] having devoured of you the living with prostitutes, came, you have killed for him the fattened calf.

en.L: But when this son of yours came, who devoured your living with prostitutes, you killed the fattened calf for him!'
en.B: But this son of yours has eaten up your property with prostitutes, and the moment he turns up, you slaughter the fattened calf for him!'
en.R: But now this son of yours comes home. He wasted your money on prostitutes. And you killed the fat calf for him!'

es.L: Pero cuando vino este hijo tuyo, el que devoró tu sustento con prostitutas, mataste para él el ternero cebado”.
es.B: Pero este hijo tuyo se ha comido tus bienes con prostitutas, y en cuanto aparece, ¡matas para él el ternero cebado!”.
es.R: Pero ahora vuelve a casa este hijo tuyo. Malgastó tu dinero con prostitutas. ¡Y tú mataste para él el ternero gordo!”.

fr.L: Mais quand ton fils que voici est venu, lui qui a dévoré ton bien avec des prostituées, tu as tué pour lui le veau gras !”
fr.B: Mais ton fils, celui-là, a dévoré ton bien avec des prostituées, et à peine est-il revenu que tu tues pour lui le veau gras !”
fr.R: Mais maintenant, ton fils que voilà revient à la maison. Il a gaspillé ton argent avec des prostituées. Et toi, tu as tué le veau gras pour lui !”

sw.L: Lakini alipokuja huyu mwanao, yule aliyeitafuna riziki yako pamoja na makahaba, ulimchinjia ndama aliyenenepeshwa!'
sw.B: Lakini huyu mwanao amezila mali zako pamoja na makahaba, na mara tu anapotokea, wewe unamchinjia ndama aliyenenepeshwa!'
sw.R: Lakini sasa huyu mwanao anarudi nyumbani. Alipoteza fedha zako kwa makahaba. Nawe ukamchinjia ndama mnono!'

vi.L: Nhưng khi đứa con trai này của cha về, là đứa đã nuốt hết của cải cha với bọn gái điếm, thì cha lại làm thịt con bê béo cho nó!'
vi.B: Còn thằng con này của cha đã phung phí hết tài sản của cha với bọn gái điếm, vậy mà vừa về tới là cha làm thịt con bê vỗ béo cho nó!'
vi.R: Nhưng bây giờ thằng con này của cha về nhà. Nó đã tiêu phí tiền bạc của cha với bọn gái điếm. Vậy mà cha lại làm thịt con bê béo cho nó!'

decisions.choice: this son of yours: said with scorn
decisions.reason: He will not call him "my brother". The father answers with "this brother of yours" (15:32).

decisions.choice: devoured your living: used up the family's property like a glutton
decisions.reason: To devour property is to waste it greedily. The "living" is the father's property (15:12), and he speaks of it as the father's, not his brother's share.

decisions.choice: with prostitutes: the elder son's charge
alternatives: a fact the story has already told
decisions.reason: The story said only that the younger son lived wastefully (15:13). This is the elder son's account of it.

decisions.choice: two statements, then the complaint
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable break up the sentence and keep its angry tone.

decisions.choice: his words close here
decisions.reason: The elder son's speech ends.

decisions.choice: ton fils que voici (L); ton fils, celui-là (B); ton fils que voilà (R)
decisions.reason: The elder son keeps his distance from his brother (m1). French marks the scorn with "que voici" or "celui-là", which also lets the father answer with "ton frère que voici" in 15:32 (m2).

decisions.choice: "đứa con trai này của cha" (L); "thằng con này của cha" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says "this son of yours" is said with scorn; "thằng" carries it in Vietnamese, and "của cha" keeps him from calling the man his brother.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Τέκνον, σὺ πάντοτε μετ’ ἐμοῦ εἶ, καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐμὰ σά ἐστιν·

records.literal_gloss: He and said to him, Child, you always with me are, and all that [is] mine yours is.

en.L: And he said to him, 'Child, you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours.
en.B: His father answered, 'My child, you are with me always, and all that is mine belongs to you.
en.R: The father said, 'My dear son, you have been with me the whole time. All I own is yours.

es.L: Y él le dijo: “Hijo, tú estás siempre conmigo, y todo lo mío es tuyo.
es.B: Su padre le respondió: “Hijo mío, tú estás conmigo siempre, y todo lo que tengo te pertenece.
es.R: El padre le dijo: “Mi querido hijo, tú has estado conmigo todo el tiempo. Todo lo que tengo es tuyo.

fr.L: Et il lui a dit : “Enfant, toi, tu es toujours avec moi, et tout ce qui est à moi est à toi.
fr.B: Son père lui a répondu : “Mon enfant, tu es toujours avec moi, et tout ce que j’ai t’appartient.
fr.R: Le père lui a dit : “Mon cher fils, tu as toujours été avec moi. Tout ce que je possède est à toi.

sw.L: Naye akamwambia, 'Mtoto [wangu], wewe daima uko pamoja nami, na kila kilicho changu ni chako.
sw.B: Baba yake alimjibu, 'Mwanangu, wewe uko nami wakati wote, na yote niliyo nayo ni mali yako.
sw.R: Baba alisema, 'Mwanangu mpendwa, umekuwa pamoja nami muda wote. Kila kitu nilicho nacho ni chako.

vi.L: Và người cha nói với anh: 'Con ơi, con luôn luôn ở với cha, và mọi thứ của cha đều là của con.
vi.B: Người cha trả lời: 'Con ơi, con lúc nào cũng ở với cha, và mọi thứ của cha đều là của con.
vi.R: Người cha nói: 'Con yêu dấu của cha, con đã luôn ở bên cha. Tất cả những gì cha có đều là của con.

decisions.choice: child: a tender way to address a son
alternatives: a rebuke, as to a small child
decisions.reason: The word means child. The father speaks gently, even after his son's angry words.

decisions.choice: all that is mine is yours: the rest of the property belongs to him already
decisions.reason: The father divided his property between both sons (15:12). The elder son has lost nothing by his brother's return.

decisions.choice: My dear son
decisions.reason: Readable gives the warmth of the word as a father would say it.

decisions.choice: his words open here and run on to 15:32
decisions.reason: The father's answer is one speech.

decisions.choice: Hijo
decisions.reason: A tender way to address a son (meaning decision m1). Spanish "hijo" is the word a parent uses for a child of any age; "niño" would make the grown son sound small.

decisions.choice: "Con ơi" (L, B); "Con yêu dấu của cha" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says "child" is a tender address; "Con ơi" is the warm Vietnamese call, and Readable says the love plainly, as the English Readable does.

source.text: εὐφρανθῆναι δὲ καὶ χαρῆναι ἔδει, ὅτι ὁ ἀδελφός σου οὗτος νεκρὸς ἦν καὶ ἔζησεν, καὶ ἀπολωλὼς καὶ εὑρέθη.

records.literal_gloss: To make merry however and to rejoice it was fitting, because the brother of you this dead was and is alive, and was lost and is found.

en.L: But it was necessary to celebrate and rejoice, because this brother of yours was dead and has come to life, and [was] lost and has been found.'"
en.B: But it was only right to celebrate and rejoice, for this brother of yours was dead and has come to life; he was lost and has been found.'"
en.R: It was right for us to have a party and be glad. Your brother was dead, and now he lives again! He was lost, and now he has been found!'"

es.L: Pero era preciso celebrar y regocijarse, porque este hermano tuyo estaba muerto y volvió a vivir, y [estaba] perdido y fue hallado”».
es.B: Pero lo justo era celebrar y alegrarse, porque este hermano tuyo estaba muerto y ha vuelto a vivir; estaba perdido y ha sido encontrado”».
es.R: Era justo que hiciéramos una fiesta y nos alegráramos. ¡Tu hermano estaba muerto, y ahora vive otra vez! ¡Estaba perdido, y ahora ha aparecido!”».

fr.L: Mais il fallait faire la fête et se réjouir, parce que ton frère que voici était mort et il est revenu à la vie, et [il était] perdu et il a été retrouvé.” »
fr.B: Mais il était juste de faire la fête et de se réjouir, car ton frère que voilà était mort, et il est revenu à la vie ; il était perdu, et il est retrouvé.” »
fr.R: Il fallait bien faire une fête et être heureux. Ton frère était mort, et maintenant il est de nouveau vivant ! Il était perdu, et maintenant on l’a retrouvé !” »

sw.L: Lakini ilikuwa lazima kusherehekea na kufurahi, kwa sababu huyu ndugu yako alikuwa mfu, naye amekuwa hai, na [alikuwa] amepotea, naye amepatikana.'"
sw.B: Lakini ilistahili kabisa kusherehekea na kufurahi, kwa sababu ndugu yako huyu alikuwa amekufa, naye amekuwa hai tena; alikuwa amepotea, naye amepatikana.'"
sw.R: Ilikuwa sawa sisi kufanya sherehe na kufurahi. Ndugu yako alikuwa amekufa, na sasa yu hai tena! Alikuwa amepotea, na sasa amepatikana!'"

vi.L: Nhưng phải ăn mừng và vui vẻ, vì đứa em này của con đã chết mà nay sống lại, đã mất mà nay đã tìm thấy.'"
vi.B: Nhưng chúng ta phải ăn mừng và vui vẻ mới đúng, vì đứa em này của con đã chết mà nay sống lại, đã mất mà nay lại tìm được.'"
vi.R: Chúng ta phải mở tiệc và vui mừng mới phải. Em con đã chết, mà nay lại sống! Nó đã bị mất, mà nay đã được tìm thấy!'"

decisions.choice: it was necessary: it was the only right thing to do
decisions.reason: The word means "it must be". It is the word Luke uses for what God's purpose requires (2:49; 9:22). The father could not do otherwise.

decisions.choice: this brother of yours: the father's reply to "this son of yours" (15:30)
alternatives: a plain way of naming him
decisions.reason: The father reminds the elder son that the one who came home is his brother.

decisions.choice: was dead and has come to life; was lost and has been found
decisions.reason: As in 15:24.

decisions.choice: the story ends without saying whether the elder son went in
alternatives: the elder son refused for good
decisions.reason: Jesus leaves the ending open. The listeners who grumbled in 15:2 must decide for themselves whether they will join the feast.

decisions.choice: the father's words and Jesus' speech close here
decisions.reason: The parable that began in 15:11 ends with the chapter.

decisions.choice: "đứa em này của con" (L, B)
decisions.reason: The father answers "this son of yours" (15:30) with "this brother of yours" (meaning decision); the matching "... này của con" keeps the reply audible.
